bundles.title: Bundle 1: Physical Architecture
bundles.description: Scenario questions on physical design, high availability, ArcGIS Enterprise URLs, capacity sizing, architecture adjustment and VDI for ArcGIS Pro, based on ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 and Architecture Center guidance.

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to document physical architecture that will meet nonfunctional requirements
questions.question: A regional council is moving its ArcGIS Enterprise deployment onto its existing VMware cluster. The project sponsor asks you to document a production hardware specification for each VM before any software is installed. According to Esri's recommended approach to modern physical design, how should you arrive at the production specification?
answers: Start with a mid-sized profile, test a proof of concept with representative workflows while monitoring, then adjust to set the production profile
Run the Capacity Planning Toolkit with the expected user counts and order hardware that matches its calculated core and memory figures for a multi-year period
Allocate the largest VM size the cluster allows to every component, then reduce resources only if the virtualisation team reports contention after go-live
Use the minimum system requirements for each component as the production specification, because virtual machines can be resized later if users complain
questions.explanation: Esri's best-practice approach is to start with a reasonable, middle-sized profile, deploy and test a proof of concept with representative services and workflows, monitor resources and adjust, then use that evidence to define production. The Capacity Planning Toolkit is described as no longer updated and not reflective of modern web-based workflows.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Physical design considerations

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to document physical architecture that will meet nonfunctional requirements
questions.question: A utility's service level agreement for its ArcGIS Enterprise field-operations system specifies 99.9% availability measured over a year. When documenting this nonfunctional requirement, approximately how much total downtime per year does the target allow?
answers: About 8.77 hours per year
About 3.65 days per year
About 52.6 minutes per year
About 43.8 hours per year
questions.explanation: Three nines (99.9%) allows 0.1% of 8,766 hours, which is about 8.77 hours of downtime per year. Two nines (99%) would allow about 3.65 days.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: High availability

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to document physical architecture that will meet nonfunctional requirements
questions.question: A government agency's requirements state that its ArcGIS Enterprise base deployment must meet a strict uptime SLA with component-level failover. Its current design places Portal for ArcGIS, the hosting server, ArcGIS Data Store and ArcGIS Web Adaptor on one large VM protected by hypervisor host restart. What should the documented physical architecture be?
answers: A multi-machine base deployment, because component-level redundancy is only available when components are spread across machines
The single-machine deployment, because hypervisor host restart and snapshots provide equivalent component failover for each ArcGIS component
The single-machine deployment with additional vCPU and memory, because vertical scaling removes the single point of failure
A single-machine base deployment plus a separate federated ArcGIS Server site, because that pattern provides failover for the base components
questions.explanation: Esri's decision guide states that component-level redundancy is only available in a multi-machine deployment, so any HA requirement forces that topology. Host restart and infrastructure replication give resilience but not component failover, so a strict uptime SLA is not a fit for single-machine.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Decision guide: Single or multi-machine base deployment

questions.objective: Design a highly available deployment
questions.question: You are federating a two-machine ArcGIS Server site with a highly available portal. The server machines sit behind a load balancer at https://gis.example.com/server. Which value should you use as the Administration URL during federation?
answers: A load balancer URL that can reach every machine in the site, even when one machine is unavailable
The URL of the first ArcGIS Server machine on port 6443, because it was used to create the site
The URL of the portal's privatePortalURL, so that the server and portal share a single endpoint
The URL of one ArcGIS Web Adaptor instance, so that administrative traffic bypasses the load balancer
questions.explanation: The Administration URL must be one the portal can use to communicate with all servers in the site even when one is unavailable, such as a load balancer URL. If it points to a single machine and that machine goes offline, federation will not work.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: High availability in ArcGIS Enterprise
source.section: URLs used in federation — Administrative URL

questions.objective: Design a highly available deployment
questions.question: An organisation has two data centres 300 km apart. It proposes placing the primary portal, primary relational data store and one ArcGIS Server machine in data centre A, and the standby portal, standby data store and second server machine in data centre B, to survive the loss of a whole site. What is the most appropriate response?
answers: Keep all HA components in one data centre or cloud region, and protect against site loss with a separate disaster recovery deployment
Accept the design, because ArcGIS Enterprise HA uses asynchronous replication designed for geographically separated data centres
Accept the design only if the ArcGIS Server configuration store is replicated between both data centres by the storage vendor
Place the portal machines in separate data centres but keep the data store and server machines together in data centre A
questions.explanation: Esri states that HA configurations are designed for a single data centre or cloud region, and primary and standby machines should not be split across data centres. To protect against losing a data centre, create a secondary deployment as part of disaster recovery.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: High availability in ArcGIS Enterprise

questions.objective: Design a highly available deployment
questions.question: A design for a highly available ArcGIS Enterprise deployment on an on-premises hypervisor cluster has both Portal for ArcGIS VMs, both ArcGIS Server VMs and both relational data store VMs running on the same physical host to minimise network latency. What is the key flaw, and how should it be corrected?
answers: The single host is a single point of failure; use anti-affinity rules so paired VMs run on different physical hosts
The VMs will contend for CPU; set CPU reservations on the shared host so each pair receives guaranteed resources
Latency is not a concern within a cluster; move each pair to a different cloud region to improve resilience
The standby VMs waste resources; power them off and start them automatically from a template if the host fails
questions.explanation: Esri advises not to put all components of a software tier on one VM host, because that host becomes a single point of failure. Anti-affinity rules keep primary and standby VMs on separate physical hosts. Moving pairs to separate regions would conflict with the guidance to colocate HA components.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: High availability in ArcGIS Enterprise

questions.objective: Design a highly available deployment
questions.question: A highly available portal uses Integrated Windows Authentication (IWA), and all clients are internal. The design places a web adaptor in front of each portal machine. How should the hosting server machines communicate with the portal so that HA is preserved?
answers: Through a privatePortalURL on a load balancer on port 7443 that sends traffic straight to the portal machines
Through the organisation URL via the web adaptors, using a service account that holds an IWA login
Directly to the primary portal machine on port 7443, because the standby portal does not accept server requests
Through either web adaptor directly, since the web adaptors already balance requests between both portal machines
questions.explanation: Server-to-portal traffic must bypass the web-tier authentication challenge, so the load balancer listens on 7080/7443 and sends that traffic directly to the portal through the privatePortalURL. Pointing at one portal machine would break HA if that machine failed.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Highly available ArcGIS Enterprise deployment scenarios
source.section: IWA or LDAP authentication with client access internal

questions.objective: Identify the URLs used in ArcGIS Enterprise
questions.question: After you federate a multiple-machine ArcGIS Server site using the load balancer URL https://gis.example.com/server as the Administration URL, an administrator reports that https://gisserver01.example.com:6443/arcgis/manager no longer lets them manage the site. Which URL should they use?
answers: https://gis.example.com/server/manager
https://gisserver01.example.com:6080/arcgis/manager
https://gis.example.com/portal/portaladmin
https://gisserver01.example.com:6443/arcgis/admin
questions.explanation: If you federate using a load balancer URL, you must connect to ArcGIS Server Manager through the load balancer and cannot use the default machine URL on port 6443. Manager URLs through a load balancer take the form https://loadbalancerhost/webcontext/manager.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Configure highly available ArcGIS Enterprise
source.section: Configure a highly available ArcGIS Server site

questions.objective: Identify the URLs used in ArcGIS Enterprise
questions.question: A partner agency needs the WMS endpoint for a map service named Roads, stored in the Transport folder of an ArcGIS Server site accessed through a web adaptor named server at gis.example.com. Which URL is correct?
answers: https://gis.example.com/server/services/Transport/Roads/MapServer/WMSServer
https://gis.example.com/server/rest/services/Transport/Roads/MapServer/WMSServer
https://gis.example.com/server/rest/services/Transport/Roads/WMSServer
https://gis.example.com/server/sharing/rest/Transport/Roads/MapServer/WMSServer
questions.explanation: The rest constant is not used in OGC service URLs such as WMS, WMTS, WCS, WFS and WPS, so the path is /services/folder/service/MapServer/WMSServer. The /sharing/rest path belongs to the Portal Directory, not ArcGIS Server.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Components of ArcGIS URLs

questions.objective: Identify the URLs used in ArcGIS Enterprise
questions.question: A new ArcGIS Enterprise organisation will be accessed at https://maps.example.com/portal, where maps.example.com is a DNS alias assigned to an external load balancer. Portal for ArcGIS has just been installed. What must be configured before any content is created or any ArcGIS Server site is federated?
answers: Set the portal's WebContextURL to the organisation URL on the load balancer
Set the hosting server's Services URL to the load balancer's internal address
Register a second web adaptor using the portal machine's fully qualified name
Set the privatePortalURL to the portal machine's address on port 7443
questions.explanation: When the organisation URL is a DNS alias on a reverse proxy or load balancer, you must set the WebContextURL before creating content or federating a server. The privatePortalURL is for internal server-to-portal traffic and should also point to a load balancer, not a single machine.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Organization URL
source.section: DNS alias assigned to a reverse proxy or load balancer (with or without Web Adaptor in the network path)

questions.objective: Identify the URLs used in ArcGIS Enterprise
questions.question: An organisation wants to be able to upgrade ArcGIS Enterprise using a blue-green approach in future, without breaking the web maps and apps that reference its services. Which URL design best supports this?
answers: Publish a stable friendly URL such as https://maps.example.com/portal using a DNS alias that can be repointed to new infrastructure
Publish the web adaptor host's fully qualified name, such as https://giswebsrv01.prd.example.com/portal, so it is unambiguous
Publish each component's machine URL with its port, such as :7443 and :6443, so traffic skips the web tier during cutover
Publish a new versioned URL for each release, such as https://maps114.example.com/portal, and redirect users to it
questions.explanation: Esri recommends durable URLs: a stable external URL that points to the underlying infrastructure through DNS (for example a CNAME) lets you swap the backing system without changing the URL, enabling low-downtime and blue-green upgrades. Changing URLs breaks references embedded in content and apps.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: DNS, naming, and URLs

questions.objective: Given a scenario, use system design inputs to calculate required server capacities
questions.question: Monitoring shows that a heavily used dedicated-instance map service needs up to 12 instances running at the same time to keep wait times acceptable at peak. The ArcGIS Server site has 3 machines. Following Esri's guidance, what should the service's maximum number of instances be set to?
questions.explanation: Maximum instances is a per-machine setting. Esri says to divide the total number of instances needed by the number of ArcGIS Server machines: 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Setting 12 would allow up to 36 instances across the site.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Anticipate and accommodate users

questions.objective: Given a scenario, use system design inputs to calculate required server capacities
questions.question: Because of a VM limit, a design places both a relational data store and a spatiotemporal big data store on the same ArcGIS Data Store 11.4 machine, with no other ArcGIS components installed. Based on the documented minimum free memory for each data store type, how much free memory must the machine have before you configure them?
answers: 24 GB
16 GB
32 GB
8 GB
questions.explanation: The relational data store needs 8 GB and the spatiotemporal big data store needs 16 GB. If you put more than one type on a machine, it must meet the combined requirement: 8 + 16 = 24 GB. Esri also says it does not recommend combining types, and more memory is needed once the stores are in use.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: ArcGIS Data Store 11.4 system requirements

questions.objective: Given a scenario, use system design inputs to calculate required server capacities
questions.question: You export an ArcGIS Monitor report as a system design input for business hours only. The federated GIS Server machine shows P95 CPU utilisation of 94% and P95 physical memory utilisation of 62%. Users are expected to grow 30% over two years. How should you interpret this?
answers: CPU is overloaded and needs load distribution or more resources; memory has not reached the level that signals a need
Both resources are within limits, because the averages rather than the P95 values should drive capacity decisions
Memory is the constraint, because P95 memory above 60% indicates the machine needs more RAM before CPU is addressed
CPU is acceptable, because the P95 value only describes the busiest 5% of time and can be ignored for sizing
questions.explanation: Esri's guidance focuses on P95 values for peak periods: P95 CPU above 90% suggests the machine is overloaded and needs distributed load or more resources, while P95 memory above 80% suggests it needs more memory. At 62%, memory has not reached that level, although you should still allow for growth.

source.title: Esri Community: Using ArcGIS Monitor Excel Report in System Design
source.section: Machine Resources and Utilization — CPU; Memory

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to adjust architecture to meet requirements and constraints
questions.question: A federated ArcGIS Server machine hosts about 300 map services, most of which are rarely used. At peak, ArcGIS Monitor shows more than 250 ArcSOC processes running, and the site is becoming unstable. Budget rules out new hardware this year. Which change best addresses the problem?
answers: Move rarely used map services to shared instances and reduce maximum instances where over-provisioned
Raise the minimum instances on every service so that ArcSOC processes are not repeatedly created and destroyed
Convert all map services to dedicated instances so that each service has guaranteed processes available
Increase the idle timeout for all services so instances are kept running longer between requests
questions.explanation: Esri notes that more than 200 service instances at peak can threaten site stability. It recommends tuning maximum instances and moving less-used map and feature services to shared instances, which pool ArcSOC processes and save memory. Raising minimums or idle timeouts would increase the process count.

source.title: Esri Community: Using ArcGIS Monitor Excel Report in System Design

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to adjust architecture to meet requirements and constraints
questions.question: Under representative load, feature service response times degrade. ArcGIS Server CPU and memory stay healthy, but enterprise geodatabase query latency rises sharply. The infrastructure team proposes adding two more ArcGIS Server machines. What is the most appropriate recommendation?
answers: Investigate the data tier first, because ArcGIS Server is not the measured bottleneck
Add the two machines, because scaling out increases aggregate capacity and will reduce database latency
Scale up the existing ArcGIS Server machines with more vCPU, because that avoids topology changes
Increase the maximum instances on the feature services so more database connections can run in parallel
questions.explanation: Esri's scaling decision guide says to measure the bottleneck before scaling. Where ArcGIS Server CPU and memory remain healthy while database latency rises, the recommendation is to investigate other bottlenecks, because the server tier is not the constraint.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Decision guide: Scale with added capacity or machines

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to adjust architecture to meet requirements and constraints
questions.question: A virtualisation team offers 8 vCPUs for an ArcGIS Server site on its on-premises hypervisor and suggests four VMs with 2 vCPUs each to spread risk. There is no high-availability requirement for this site. Based on Esri guidance for ArcGIS Server on virtualised hardware, what should you recommend?
answers: One VM with 8 vCPUs, because a few large VMs perform better than many small ones
Four VMs with 2 vCPUs each, because more machines always increases ArcGIS Server throughput
Eight VMs with 1 vCPU each, so each ArcSOC process is isolated on its own machine
Two VMs with 4 vCPUs each, because ArcGIS Server requires a minimum of two machines per site
questions.explanation: Esri recommends using a few large VMs rather than many small ones; for example, a single VM with eight CPUs performs better than four VMs with two CPUs each. ArcGIS Server sites can run on a single machine.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Deploy ArcGIS Server on virtualized hardware

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine which VDI configuration to use
questions.question: An organisation already delivers ArcMap to 40 users through Remote Desktop Session Host (RDSH) on a GPU-equipped Windows Server. It plans to deliver ArcGIS Pro with 2D and 3D work to the same users the same way. What is the main concern Esri identifies with this approach?
answers: There is no hypervisor-level vGPU manager, so sessions compete for GPU memory and time
RDSH cannot run ArcGIS Pro at all, because ArcGIS Pro only installs on Windows client operating systems
RDSH requires GPU pass-through to each session, which limits the server to one ArcGIS Pro user per GPU
RDSH forces ArcGIS Pro to use OpenGL instead of DirectX, which disables 3D scene rendering
questions.explanation: Esri states that RDSH is not designed to deliver 3D applications. Without a vGPU manager at the hypervisor level to schedule GPU time or manage GPU memory between sessions, sessions consume the GPU until it is exhausted, and performance degrades for everyone on the server.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro 3.4: ArcGIS Pro in a virtualized environment

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine which VDI configuration to use
questions.question: A Citrix customer wants to deliver ArcGIS Pro on-premises and asks whether to publish it as a Citrix Virtual Apps application or to provide VDI desktops. Which configuration aligns with Esri guidance?
answers: VDI virtual machines, such as Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops, with NVIDIA vGPU or pass-through GPU
Citrix Virtual Apps on a CPU-only host, because ArcGIS Pro falls back to software rendering
Citrix Virtual Apps with a shared GPU, because application virtualisation gives the highest user density
VDI virtual machines without a GPU, provided each VM has at least 32 GB RAM and 8 vCPUs
questions.explanation: Esri says on-premises virtualisation must provide shared (virtual) or pass-through GPUs through VDI VMs, and that Citrix Virtual Apps is not recommended because it cannot provide adequate GPU resources to ArcGIS Pro.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro 3.4: On-Premises virtualization

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine which VDI configuration to use
questions.question: A VDI design must support two user groups: about 60 analysts doing mostly 2D editing, and 4 specialists who build large 3D scenes and need the best possible graphics performance. Which GPU configuration best fits the 3D specialists?
answers: Pass-through GPUs dedicated to their VMs, accepting reduced host scalability
A shared vGPU profile identical to the analysts', to maximise user density
No GPU, with extra vCPUs added so the CPU can render 3D scenes
An RDSH session host with one GPU shared by all four specialists
questions.explanation: Passing a whole GPU through to a VM gives optimal performance for 3D power users but reduces the scalability of the VM host. A shared vGPU suits users who need sufficient graphics performance at higher density, such as the 2D analysts.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro 3.4: ArcGIS Pro in a virtualized environment

bundles.title: Bundle 2: Solution Architecture
bundles.description: Scenario questions on choosing ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 components, server roles, data store types and authentication methods, and on adapting a design to meet constraints.

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS components that will be required in the design
questions.question: A regional council is starting with a base ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 deployment. Which set of components makes up the minimum base deployment described by Esri?
answers: Portal for ArcGIS; ArcGIS GIS Server as hosting server; ArcGIS Data Store as relational and object store; two ArcGIS Web Adaptors
Portal for ArcGIS; ArcGIS GIS Server as hosting server; ArcGIS Data Store as relational and tile cache store; one ArcGIS Web Adaptor
Portal for ArcGIS; ArcGIS Image Server as hosting server; ArcGIS Data Store as relational store only; two ArcGIS Web Adaptors
Portal for ArcGIS; ArcGIS GIS Server as hosting server; an enterprise geodatabase as hosting data store; two ArcGIS Web Adaptors
questions.explanation: At 11.4 the base deployment is a portal, a GIS Server hosting server, ArcGIS Data Store configured as a relational data store and an object store, and two Web Adaptors (one for the portal, one for the hosting server). The tile cache data store is no longer used for new hosted scene layer caches at 11.4; the object store replaces it.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Base ArcGIS Enterprise deployment

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS components that will be required in the design
questions.question: A utility must expose an ArcGIS Server site to external users through its standard HTTPS port and site name, hide the default ArcGIS Server port and 'arcgis' site name, and block ArcGIS Server Manager and the Administrator Directory from external users. Which component best meets these requirements?
answers: ArcGIS Web Adaptor deployed in the organisation's web server
A second federated ArcGIS GIS Server site in the perimeter network
ArcGIS Data Store configured as a standby relational data store
Portal for ArcGIS configured with a built-in identity store
questions.explanation: ArcGIS Web Adaptor integrates ArcGIS Server with an existing web server, presents the site on the organisation's standard port and name, and can block ArcGIS Server Manager and the Administrator Directory from external users. Adding another GIS Server site does not change how the existing site is exposed.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Use ArcGIS Web Adaptor

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS components that will be required in the design
questions.question: A design adds ArcGIS Notebook Server so analysts can author Python notebooks in the portal. Which additional component must the architect include on each ArcGIS Notebook Server machine?
answers: A container engine, either Mirantis Container Runtime or Docker
A local ArcGIS Data Store spatiotemporal big data store instance
ArcGIS Pro, to provide ArcPy to the notebook runtimes
A dedicated ArcGIS Web Adaptor (Java Platform) instance
questions.explanation: ArcGIS Notebook Server isolates each author in containers managed by a third-party container engine; Mirantis Container Runtime or Docker must be installed before ArcGIS Notebook Server. A web adaptor can be placed in front of the site but the Java edition is not a requirement, and the runtimes already include ArcPy.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Introduction to ArcGIS Notebook Server

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS components that will be required in the design
questions.question: Portal members at a forestry company want to publish hosted imagery layers from aerial photography. The current deployment is a base deployment only. What must be added to the design?
answers: A federated ArcGIS Image Server site with a registered file share or cloud store
An ArcGIS Data Store object store, which stores the hosted imagery layer pixels
A second ArcGIS GIS Server site configured as an additional hosting server
An ArcGIS Data Store spatiotemporal big data store to hold raster tiles
questions.explanation: Hosted image layers run on a federated ArcGIS Image Server site rather than the hosting server, and their data is copied to a registered file or cloud storage data store, not to a data store created with ArcGIS Data Store. Neither the object store nor the spatiotemporal big data store holds hosted imagery.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: ArcGIS Data Store vocabulary
source.section: hosted web layers; ArcGIS Image Server

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS Server roles/extensions that will be required in the design
questions.question: To save on infrastructure, a project team proposes making its existing federated ArcGIS Image Server site the portal's hosting server so members can publish hosted feature layers. What should the architect advise?
answers: The hosting server must be an ArcGIS Server site licensed as ArcGIS GIS Server
The proposal works if the Image Server site also has a relational data store
The proposal works if the Image Server site is set as raster analysis server
The hosting server must be an ArcGIS Server site licensed as GeoEvent Server
questions.explanation: Esri states that a portal's hosting server must be licensed as an ArcGIS GIS Server site to publish the service types that hosted web layers require. Registering a relational data store or assigning the raster analysis role does not change the licensing role of an Image Server site.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: ArcGIS Data Store vocabulary

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS Server roles/extensions that will be required in the design
questions.question: In a base deployment, the hosting server also runs many map services that reference enterprise geodatabases, and both hosted-layer and map performance is suffering. Which design change does Esri describe as a common way to address this?
answers: Federate a separate ArcGIS GIS Server site dedicated to mapping and referenced services
Install ArcGIS GIS Server on the ArcGIS Data Store machine to share the processing
Re-license the hosting server as ArcGIS Image Server to enable distributed processing
Federate an ArcGIS Workflow Manager Server site to queue the map service requests
questions.explanation: The GIS Server in a base deployment acts as both hosting server and general-purpose server; many organisations split these into two ArcGIS Server sites, adding a federated GIS Server site dedicated to mapping and visualisation. Workflow Manager Server manages work, not map request load.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: ArcGIS Enterprise server roles

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS Server roles/extensions that will be required in the design
questions.question: An investigations unit wants to model and analyse relationships between people, vehicles, properties and events as knowledge graph layers in ArcGIS Enterprise. Which addition to the base deployment is required?
answers: An ArcGIS Knowledge Server site plus an ArcGIS Data Store graph store on its own machine
An ArcGIS Notebook Server site plus an ArcGIS Data Store graph store on the portal machine
An ArcGIS Knowledge Server site plus an ArcGIS Data Store spatiotemporal big data store
An ArcGIS GeoEvent Server site plus an ArcGIS Data Store relational data store
questions.explanation: Knowledge graph layers run on a federated ArcGIS Knowledge Server site, which also requires ArcGIS Data Store configured as a graph store installed on its own machine. The spatiotemporal big data store does not hold knowledge graph entities and relationships.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: ArcGIS Enterprise server roles

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS Server roles/extensions that will be required in the design
questions.question: A national science agency serves dynamic image services from mosaic datasets to many users and regularly runs raster analysis on very large datasets. What ArcGIS Image Server deployment pattern does Esri recommend?
answers: Separate ArcGIS Image Server sites for raster analysis and for dynamic image services
One large ArcGIS Image Server site performing raster analysis and dynamic services
Several ArcGIS Image Server sites, each designated as a raster analysis server
Raster analysis on the hosting server, with dynamic services on an Image Server site
questions.explanation: Where raster analysis regularly runs on large datasets, Esri recommends separate sites for raster analysis and dynamic image services so the image services are not affected. Only one ArcGIS Image Server site can be dedicated to raster analytics in a deployment, so several raster analysis sites is not valid.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: ArcGIS Enterprise server roles

questions.objective: Identify appropriate Data Store types
questions.question: After upgrading to ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4, a city wants members to publish new hosted scene layers from ArcGIS Pro. Which ArcGIS Data Store type must be available to hold the scene layer caches?
answers: Object store
Tile cache data store
Relational data store
Spatiotemporal big data store
questions.explanation: Starting with 11.4, publishing hosted scene layers requires an object store for the layer caches. The tile cache data store only holds caches for scene layers published at 11.3 or earlier, and Esri recommends migrating those caches to the object store.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: ArcGIS Data Store vocabulary
source.section: object store; tile cache data store

questions.objective: Identify appropriate Data Store types
questions.question: A transport operator will use ArcGIS GeoEvent Server to process vehicle positions at about 1,500 events per second and must archive every observation for later analysis. Which data store should the design use for the archive?
answers: A multi-machine spatiotemporal big data store registered with the hosting server
The relational data store already registered with the portal's hosting server
An object store configured in cluster mode for high-velocity event archiving
A graph store registered with the hosting server to hold the event history
questions.explanation: A spatiotemporal big data store (Esri's example uses three nodes) enables high-velocity, large-volume archiving of GeoEvent Server data. The relational data store handles event volumes below 200 events per second, so it is unsuitable at 1,500 events per second.

questions.objective: Identify appropriate Data Store types
questions.question: A roading contractor plans to enable location sharing in its ArcGIS Enterprise organisation so field crews' positions are recorded from ArcGIS Field Maps. Which ArcGIS Data Store type does this require?
answers: Spatiotemporal big data store
Relational data store
Object store
Graph store
questions.explanation: Esri's functionality table lists location sharing, and apps that rely on it such as ArcGIS Field Maps and ArcGIS Indoors, as requiring the spatiotemporal big data store. The relational data store supports hosted feature layers but is not the listed requirement for location sharing.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Apps and functionality that require ArcGIS Data Store

questions.objective: Identify appropriate Data Store types
questions.question: An ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 deployment runs on Microsoft Azure virtual machines. The operations team wants an object store for 3D tiles and scene layer caches but does not want to manage extra ArcGIS Data Store machines. Which option is supported?
answers: Register Azure Blob Storage as the deployment's single object store
Register Azure Blob Storage as a second object store beside Data Store
Use the relational data store, which also holds caches when on Azure
Use Azure Files as a tile cache data store for all new scene layers
questions.explanation: When ArcGIS Enterprise runs in AWS or Azure, the object store can be provided by Amazon S3 or Azure Blob Storage instead of ArcGIS Data Store. Only one object store is supported per deployment, so running a cloud object store alongside a Data Store object store is not valid.

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine authentication methods based on business needs
questions.question: Following a merger, a company's staff accounts sit in two separate Active Directory forests. All staff must sign in to the ArcGIS Enterprise portal with their existing corporate credentials. Which authentication approach should the architect specify?
answers: Configure a SAML identity provider that can authenticate users from both forests
Configure Integrated Windows Authentication against the first forest's domain
Configure portal-tier authentication with both forests as Active Directory stores
Configure LDAP web-tier authentication with ArcGIS Web Adaptor (Java Platform)
questions.explanation: With an Active Directory identity store, ArcGIS Enterprise supports multiple domains within a single forest but not cross-forest authentication; Esri states a SAML identity provider is required to support users from multiple forests. IWA and portal-tier Active Directory configurations are bound by the same single-forest limit.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Portal authentication configuration

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine authentication methods based on business needs
questions.question: A government department wants staff signed in to the portal automatically with their Windows domain logon, with no extra sign-in prompt. The infrastructure team has proposed ArcGIS Web Adaptor (Java Platform) on Apache Tomcat. What should the architect specify?
answers: Integrated Windows Authentication with ArcGIS Web Adaptor (IIS) on Microsoft IIS
Integrated Windows Authentication with the proposed Web Adaptor (Java Platform)
Portal-tier authentication against Active Directory on the Tomcat web adaptor
Built-in identity store with accounts named to match the Windows usernames
questions.explanation: IWA gives users automatic sign-in with their Windows accounts, but it requires ArcGIS Web Adaptor (IIS) on Microsoft IIS; Web Adaptor (Java Platform) cannot perform IWA. Portal-tier authentication requires users to enter credentials each time, so it does not meet the single sign-on need.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Use Integrated Windows Authentication

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine authentication methods based on business needs
questions.question: A district council has no SAML identity provider. It needs Active Directory staff and built-in contractor accounts to sign in to the same portal, and public maps shared with everyone must stay available anonymously. Which approach meets these needs, and what is the trade-off?
answers: Portal-tier authentication with Active Directory; staff must enter credentials at each sign-in
Web-tier IWA with Active Directory; contractors are signed in automatically through IIS
PKI client-certificate authentication; anonymous users are issued a guest certificate
Web-tier LDAP authentication; built-in accounts are synchronised into the LDAP directory
questions.explanation: Portal-tier authentication lets users sign in with either organisation-specific or built-in credentials without SAML, and permits anonymous access to content shared with everyone. The trade-off is that automatic sign-on is not available, so organisation-specific users enter their credentials each time.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Portal authentication configuration

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine authentication methods based on business needs
questions.question: A security agency requires smart card (PKI client-certificate) authentication to its portal. The communications team also wants to embed public web maps from that same portal on the agency's public website. Which constraint must the architect raise?
answers: Anonymous access to the portal cannot be enabled when client-certificate authentication is used
Client-certificate authentication requires ArcGIS Web Adaptor (Java Platform) in every case
Client-certificate authentication can only be used with the portal's built-in identity store
Public maps must be shared to a SAML group before anonymous viewers can access them
questions.explanation: Esri states it is not possible to enable anonymous access to the portal when using client-certificate authentication, so public maps would need another delivery approach. PKI can use Active Directory with Web Adaptor (IIS) or LDAP with the Java Platform edition, so the Java-only option is incorrect.

questions.objective: Adjust architectural solution to meet constraints
questions.question: A client asks for ArcGIS Enterprise high availability with the primary portal in one data centre and the standby portal in a second data centre 300 km away, to protect against losing a whole site. How should the architect adjust the design?
answers: Keep HA components within one data centre and add a disaster recovery strategy for site loss
Split the portal pair across sites, but keep both relational data stores in one data centre
Split every HA pair across the two data centres and add a global load balancer in front
Deploy three portal machines, one per site plus a witness, so the portal tolerates site loss
questions.explanation: ArcGIS Enterprise high-availability configurations are designed for a single data centre or equivalent (such as one cloud region) and are not designed to span data centres. To protect against losing the entire deployment, Esri advises combining high availability with disaster recovery, such as offsite backups or a standby deployment.

questions.objective: Adjust architectural solution to meet constraints
questions.question: To keep the server count low, a draft design puts the relational data store, object store and spatiotemporal big data store on one ArcGIS Data Store machine. What should the architect recommend?
answers: Place each data store type on separate machines so they do not compete for memory and disk
Keep them on one machine but give the object store a dedicated disk for its content directory
Keep them on one machine, since ArcGIS Data Store shares one configuration store for all types
Move the spatiotemporal big data store onto the hosting server machine to balance the load
questions.explanation: Esri advises configuring each required ArcGIS Data Store type on separate machines, because each type can need a large share of memory and disk and they compete when co-located. Each data store type also has its own configuration store, so the shared configuration store reasoning is wrong.

questions.objective: Adjust architectural solution to meet constraints
questions.question: A network security team wants all traffic from a new ArcGIS GIS Server site to the portal routed through a forward proxy and limited to port 443. The site must be federated with the portal. How should the architect respond?
answers: Federation needs direct network access from the server site to the portal over port 7443
Federation works through the forward proxy if the portal's Web Adaptor listens on port 443
Federation works if the server site's administration URL is set to the forward proxy URL
Federation needs direct access from the portal to the server site over port 6080 only
questions.explanation: To federate successfully, the ArcGIS Server site must have direct network access to the portal over port 7443, and a forward proxy cannot manage or direct traffic between the server and portal. The firewall and proxy design must be adjusted to allow this.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Federate a server site

questions.objective: Adjust architectural solution to meet constraints
questions.question: A government agency has standardised on Linux for its ArcGIS Server machines, but its web tier is managed by a team that only supports Microsoft IIS on Windows. Which design meets both constraints?
answers: Deploy ArcGIS Web Adaptor (IIS) on the Windows web servers in front of the Linux site
Move ArcGIS Server to Windows, as Web Adaptor must match the server's platform
Deploy ArcGIS Web Adaptor (Java Platform) on the Linux ArcGIS Server machines
Omit Web Adaptor and expose ArcGIS Server directly to clients on port 6443
questions.explanation: ArcGIS Web Adaptor is platform independent of ArcGIS Server, so a Linux ArcGIS Server site can use ArcGIS Web Adaptor (IIS). Deploying the Java Platform edition would not satisfy the IIS-only web tier constraint, and exposing port 6443 directly loses the Web Adaptor benefits.

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to select an upgrade strategy
questions.question: A regional council runs a base deployment of ArcGIS Enterprise 10.7.1 and wants to reach ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 while keeping its existing content and configuration. Which upgrade path is supported?
answers: Upgrade to an interim release between 10.8.x and 11.3, then upgrade that release to 11.4
Run the 11.4 setups directly over 10.7.1, because the setups detect any earlier installation
Uninstall 10.7.1, install 11.4 clean, then restore the old webgisdr backup into it
Upgrade to 10.9.1 first, then to 11.0, and only then run the 11.4 setups
questions.explanation: Direct upgrades to 11.4 from 10.7 or 10.7.1 are not supported; you must first upgrade to an interim version (10.8.x to 11.3). The setups only upgrade supported prior versions in place, and you don't need to step through every release in sequence.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Upgrade ArcGIS Enterprise

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to select an upgrade strategy
questions.question: A three-machine ArcGIS Server site sits behind a load balancer. While upgrading it to 11.4, which approach follows the documented procedure?
answers: Upgrade machines one at a time and run Continue Server Upgrade locally or on port 6443
Run setup on all machines at once, then click Continue Server Upgrade through the load balancer
Upgrade one machine, then rejoin the other machines to the site after a clean 11.4 install
Upgrade machines one at a time and run Continue Server Upgrade through the Web Adaptor URL
questions.explanation: Esri recommends upgrading each machine sequentially and waiting for one to finish before continuing on the next. Continue Server Upgrade must be run in Server Manager on the local machine, or on the machine's FQDN on port 6443. It cannot be completed through a Web Adaptor or load balancer.

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to select an upgrade strategy
questions.question: You are upgrading a highly available Portal for ArcGIS deployment to 11.4. Setup has finished on both portal machines, and you started Continue portal upgrade on the standby machine. Where should you run the post-upgrade operation?
answers: On the same machine where the upgrade operation was started
On whichever machine is currently the primary portal machine
On both portal machines, one after the other, starting with the primary
On the Web Adaptor machine, once it has been reconfigured with the portal
questions.explanation: Esri states that the postupgrade operation must be run on the same machine (primary or standby) where the upgrade operation was started; after that you can run a health check on both machines. You don't need to know which machine is primary to start the upgrade.

questions.objective: Identify potential system integration issues
questions.question: A portal and its hosting server are being upgraded from 11.1 to 11.4. To limit outage scope, the project team proposes leaving two other federated sites at 11.1: a GIS Server site used for map services, and an ArcGIS Image Server site configured as the raster analysis server. Which part of this plan is unsupported?
answers: Leaving the raster analysis Image Server site at 11.1
Leaving the GIS Server site for map services at 11.1
Leaving both of the federated sites at 11.1
Neither, as any federated site may be one release behind
questions.explanation: A prior-version federated site is supported only for a GIS Server site that is not the hosting server, or an Image Server site that is not a Raster Analytics or Image Hosting site. Raster Analytics sites must match the portal version, so the non-hosting GIS Server site may stay at 11.1 but the raster analysis site may not.

source.title: Portal for ArcGIS 11.4: Federate a server site

questions.objective: Identify potential system integration issues
questions.question: Federating a new ArcGIS Server site fails. The administration URL uses a wildcard certificate issued by the organisation's internal domain certificate authority (CA), and the certificate does not list the server hostname as a SAN. What is the most likely fix?
answers: Import the domain CA's root and intermediate certificates into the portal before federating
Change the services URL to use internal port 6080 so that federation skips TLS certificate validation
Disable the primary site administrator account so the portal's security store takes over
Configure a forward proxy on the server so requests to the portal are re-signed
questions.explanation: The administration URL's TLS certificate must either be trusted by the organisation or contain the hostname as the CN or a SAN. A wildcard certificate from a domain CA usually meets neither condition, so you must import the root (and any intermediate) certificate. Forward proxies between the server and portal are not supported for federation.

source.title: Portal for ArcGIS 11.4: Federate a server site

questions.objective: Identify potential system integration issues
questions.question: A stand-alone ArcGIS Server 11.4 site has its security configured to use Integrated Windows Authentication (IWA). An administrator tries to register the site in ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1 and registration fails. What is the cause?
answers: Monitor requires ArcGIS Server token-based security, and IWA is not supported
Monitor can register only federated sites, so the stand-alone site is rejected
The Monitor user lacks the Viewer role, which is needed to register components
Monitor Agent must first be installed on the portal machine, not on the server
questions.explanation: Registering ArcGIS Server in Monitor requires ArcGIS Server token-based security; IWA and SAML are not supported. Both stand-alone and federated sites can be registered, and registration requires the Administrator or Manager role, not Viewer.

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: A System Log Parser Statistics tab shows two services. Service A has a P95 of 0.3 s and a Max of 9.0 s. Service B has a P95 of 2.1 s and a Max of 3.0 s. Following Esri's guidance for the report, which service do you tune first?
answers: Service B, because its P95 shows most of its requests are slower than 0.5 s
Service A, because its Max shows the single slowest draw time of any service
Service A, because a large gap between P95 and Max signals instance saturation
Neither, because Avg rather than P95 or Max is the basis for tuning priority
questions.explanation: P95 is the value that 95% of responses fall under, so it reflects the experience of most users. Esri's System Log Parser guidance highlights P95 and Max values over half a second and recommends getting P95 below 0.5 s first. A single high Max value affects only a small share of requests.

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: You run eGDB Health against a versioned enterprise geodatabase. The state tree PNG shows the Default version node (red) far removed from State Zero (green). How should you interpret this?
answers: Returning the Default version, the most-used version, is costly for the database
Many versions are stale, but this has no effect on the cost of querying the Default version
The geodatabase has missing spatial indexes on the tables that are versioned
The version tree is flat and healthy, and no compress or reconcile is needed
questions.explanation: In the eGDB Health state tree schematic, the further Default is from State Zero, the more expensive it is for the database to return Default, usually the most-used version. Version staleness is shown separately in the colour-coded version tree PNG.

source.title: Esri Community: What is Egdbhealth?

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: eGDB Health has produced its output folder for a SQL Server geodatabase. You have limited time and want to address the most serious problems first. Where should you start?
answers: The Criticals column of the Expert Excel file's overview sheet
The Context Excel file's green rows containing SQL statements
The HTML file describing the RDBMS and connection metadata
The Informationals column of the Expert Excel file's overview sheet
questions.explanation: The Expert Excel file holds the evaluative findings, classified as Critical, Warning and Informational, and Esri advises reviewing the Criticals first. The Context file is descriptive rather than evaluative. Its green rows are optional, often expensive SQL queries for deeper investigation.

source.title: Esri Community: Using Egdbhealth to Evaluate a Geodatabase

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: Before a migration, you need Excel output that shows which workspaces and datasets each ArcGIS Server service uses, the portal content and users, and TLS certificate expiry dates. Which tool produces this?
answers: GIS Enterprise Reporter run with administrative credentials
System Log Parser run in Complete analysis mode for a week
eGDB Health run against each registered enterprise geodatabase
The webgisdr utility run in export mode with a full backup
questions.explanation: GIS Enterprise Reporter uses the REST admin APIs to generate Excel documentation. Its output includes a logical diagram, service inventories with workspaces and datasets, portal content, users and groups, and TLS certificate details. System Log Parser analyses service request logs, and eGDB Health evaluates a single geodatabase.

source.title: Esri Community: Introducing the GIS Enterprise Reporter

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: ArcGIS Pro users receive intermittent errors when signing in to the ArcGIS Enterprise portal, and Esri Support asks for a network trace. What is the appropriate way to capture and share it?
answers: Capture ArcGIS Pro traffic with a tool such as Fiddler, then remove tokens and credentials
Capture a HAR in browser DevTools with Preserve log on, then send it unedited for analysis
Enable Process Monitor boot logging on the client, then send the full PML trace to Support
Set the portal log level to Debug, then send the portal logs instead of any network trace
questions.explanation: ArcGIS Pro traffic happens outside the browser, so it needs a capture tool such as Fiddler rather than browser DevTools. Esri asks you to sanitise the trace by removing usernames, passwords, API keys, tokens and generateToken calls before sharing it.

source.title: Esri Support: Submit HAR Debug Files to Esri Support Services for Troubleshooting and Review

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: On an ArcGIS Server machine, a service fails to start and the server log reports only a generic access error. You suspect the ArcGIS Server account cannot read a folder or registry key. Which tool shows real-time file system, registry and process/thread activity, with filters and the user for each operation?
answers: Process Monitor
Sysmon
Fiddler
System Log Parser
questions.explanation: Process Monitor shows real-time file system, registry and process/thread activity. It includes non-destructive filtering and event properties such as user names, which makes it suited to finding access-denied operations. Sysmon is a resident service that logs events such as process creation and network connections to the Windows event log for security analysis.

source.title: Microsoft Learn: Process Monitor - Sysinternals

questions.objective: Determine which ArcGIS Monitor component to use
questions.question: You are adding a four-machine ArcGIS Server site to ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1. You want monitoring to continue if any single machine fails, and you want host metrics for every machine. Where should ArcGIS Monitor Agent be installed?
answers: On all four ArcGIS Server machines, each registered with Monitor Server
On one ArcGIS Server machine only, because it collects metrics for the site
On the Monitor Server machine only, which polls all registered components
On the Web Adaptor machine in front of the site, which sees all requests
questions.explanation: One Agent on a single server machine is the minimum. For a multi-machine site, Esri recommends installing Monitor Agent on every machine so monitoring continues after a machine failure and you get host metrics for each machine. Monitor Server is the central hub; it does not collect data itself.

source.title: ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1: Register ArcGIS Server

questions.objective: Determine which ArcGIS Monitor component to use
questions.question: The DBA team won't allow any extra software on the SQL Server machine that hosts the enterprise geodatabase. How can you still monitor the database and geodatabase in ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1?
answers: Register it from an existing Monitor Agent machine with network access to the database
Register it directly in Monitor Server, which connects to databases without an Agent
Install a second Monitor Server on a machine inside the database network segment instead
Use the Monitor database repository connection to read the geodatabase metrics
questions.explanation: Any Monitor Agent machine with access to a database can be used to register it. Installing the Agent on the database host is only recommended, to collect operating system metrics. Monitor Server is installed on a single machine, and component registration always requires an Agent.

source.title: ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1: Deployment overview

questions.objective: Determine which ArcGIS Monitor component to use
questions.question: In ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1, you want to send a periodic query to a critical feature layer and confirm that the JSON response still returns the expected feature count, not just that the service is running. What do you configure?
answers: A Check - Service observer with a regular expression on the service subcomponent
A Logs - ArcGIS Server observer with its interval shortened to one minute or less
A Request Response Time Avg alert rule with a lower critical threshold value
An Inventory - ArcGIS Server observer that scans the site for configuration changes
questions.explanation: Check - Service is an optional, user-configured observer that sends a request to an ArcGIS Server service and validates the JSON response with a regular expression. It adds metrics such as response code, response time and match count. The Logs and Inventory observers collect log entries and configuration attributes; they do not validate responses.

source.title: ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1: Register ArcGIS Server

questions.objective: Determine which ArcGIS Monitor component to use
questions.question: In ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1, you need to schedule a patching window for all production components and email reminders to the team that subscribes to them. Which Monitor capability do you use?
answers: An incident on a collection of the production components
A dataview that joins the metrics of all production components
A label applied to each component, plus an alert rule
An analysis view with a rich text element for the dates
questions.explanation: Incidents schedule maintenance tasks for a collection of monitored components, and reminder emails can be sent to the collection's subscribed users. Dataviews and analysis views are for visualising and analysing data, not for scheduling maintenance.

source.title: ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1: Introduction to ArcGIS Monitor

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: A regional council is building a standby ArcGIS Enterprise deployment in a second data centre and plans to keep it in sync with webgisdr. Before relying on it, the architect wants an Excel report of where the standby's configuration and services differ from production. Which approach suits this?
answers: Generate GIS Enterprise Reporter admin outputs for both, then run er_compare with production as File One
Generate GIS Enterprise Reporter admin outputs for both, then run er_compare with the standby as File One
Run System Log Parser against both sites for a week and compare the two Statistics worksheets
Run a webgisdr export from production and an import into the standby, then review the import log
questions.explanation: Esri's guidance names a disaster recovery site checked for webgisdr compatibility as a use case for er_compare. File One should be the reference system, such as the primary data centre, because differences are reported from File One's perspective. System Log Parser reports on service usage, not configuration.

source.title: Esri Community: Comparing ArcGIS Enterprise Systems

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: You are sizing memory for the replacement ArcGIS Server machines. You need the number of service instances that will exist as soon as ArcGIS Server starts, across the services that are running. You have run GIS Enterprise Reporter with With Analytics selected. Where do you look?
answers: The svc_analytics sheet's Total Minimum Instances Per Node (started) statistic
The svc_analytics sheet's maximum instances statistic, as all services peak together
The svc_datasets sheet, which lists the instances that each referenced dataset loads
The certificates output, which lists each machine and the services it is running
questions.explanation: The svc_analytics sheet calculates statistics for running services, and Total Minimum Instances Per Node (started) is the number of instances that exist as soon as ArcGIS Server starts. The maximum is an upper limit that is almost never reached by all services at once. The svc_datasets sheet lists datasets, not instances.

source.title: Esri Community: GIS Enterprise Reporter: Making the Most of Services Outputs

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: The GIS manager wants a System Log Parser report of service usage. IT security will not issue an ArcGIS Server account to any third-party tool, but will grant read access to the ArcGIS Server log directory through a file share. Which approach meets both needs?
answers: Run System Log Parser's ArcGIS Server (File System) log query against the shared log directory
Run System Log Parser's ArcGIS Server (Web) log query, connecting without any credentials
Run GIS Enterprise Reporter against the log share, as it reads logs without an account
Run eGDB Health as the geodatabase administrator to report on service request statistics
questions.explanation: System Log Parser can read ArcGIS Server logs directly from the file system, including over a CIFS share. Its Web log query needs publisher or administrator access to the ArcGIS Server admin endpoint. GIS Enterprise Reporter needs an administrative credential, and eGDB Health evaluates a geodatabase rather than service requests.

source.title: Esri GitHub: System Log Parser (README)

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: A SQL Server enterprise geodatabase is moving from on-premises hardware to a cloud VM. The architect wants evidence of how heavily SQL Server uses its current processors, to decide whether fewer cores could be specified. How should eGDB Health be used?
answers: Run it during a typical or peak period and review the Expert file's ProcessorUtil sheet
Run it at any time and use the logical core count in the HTML file as the cloud core count
Run it overnight to avoid load, then review the Context file's ObjClass storage sheet
Run it at any time and review the state tree PNG for the depth of the Default version
questions.explanation: The Expert Excel file's ProcessorUtil evaluation samples SQL Server's recent per-minute processor use, so it is only meaningful when run during typical or peak workload. The HTML file lists machine resources such as logical cores, but not utilisation, and logical cores may include hyperthreading.

bundles.title: Bundle 4: Architectural Concepts
bundles.description: Scenario questions on workload separation, environment isolation, distributed collaboration, content delivery, backup and disaster recovery, and tiered ArcGIS Enterprise architectures.

questions.objective: Determine when to use workload separation
questions.question: A regional council runs one ArcGIS Server site that hosts both its operational map services and a set of long-running geoprocessing services. When analysts run large geoprocessing jobs, map services used by a decision support team under an internal SLA slow noticeably. Which design change best addresses this?
answers: Create separate ArcGIS Server sites for geoprocessing and for map services, routed by a load balancer
Add more machines to the existing site so geoprocessing and map requests are spread round-robin across all machines
Configure Portal for ArcGIS for high availability so that the standby portal machine absorbs the extra load
Move the geoprocessing services into the staging environment and let analysts run their jobs there
questions.explanation: Esri recommends workload separation using multiple ArcGIS Server sites, with a load balancer routing requests by type, so a large geoprocessing task cannot starve map services and vice versa. Adding machines to one shared site still leaves both workloads competing for the same resources.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Best practices for system architecture

questions.objective: Determine when to use workload separation
questions.question: An architect is reviewing two workloads. Workload A: many editors running similar, processor-intensive editing transactions. Workload B: a mix of requests whose processing demands vary widely, from light map draws to heavy analysis. According to Esri guidance, which approach suits each workload?
answers: Workload A suits load balancing across machines; Workload B is a better candidate for workload separation
Workload A suits workload separation into dedicated sites; Workload B suits simple round-robin load balancing
Both workloads suit round-robin load balancing, because workload separation only applies to imagery services
Both workloads require workload separation, because load balancing cannot distribute editing transactions
questions.explanation: The Architecture Center states that many users running similar, processing-heavy workflows can be balanced across available hardware, while workflows with highly variable processing requirements may benefit from workload separation instead of load balancing.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Load balancing and reverse proxies

questions.objective: Determine when to use workload separation
questions.question: An organisation has separated its workloads into two ArcGIS Server sites. Site 1 runs on machines with fast, high-clock-speed processors; Site 2 runs on more modest machines. Following Esri workload separation strategy, how should requests be directed?
answers: Route CPU-intensive requests to Site 1 and lighter requests to the modest machines in Site 2
Send all requests to Site 1 first and use Site 2 only as a failover target when Site 1 becomes unavailable
Alternate all requests evenly between both sites so that each site carries the same share of the total load
Send map requests to Site 1 and all editing requests to Site 2
questions.explanation: The Architecture Center's workload separation strategy is to direct CPU-intensive requests to sites with faster processors and less intensive requests to more modest machines. Even round-robin distribution across sites ignores the different resource profiles the separation was designed for.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Workload separation

questions.objective: Design system based on environment isolation needs
questions.question: A utility is adding a staging environment in front of its production ArcGIS Enterprise deployment, but budget is tight. Which staging design aligns with Esri environment isolation guidance?
answers: Mirror production's tiers, components and server roles, possibly at reduced machine capacity
Build staging as an exact machine-for-machine clone of production, because any difference invalidates test results
Use a single all-in-one machine regardless of production's design, because staging is only used for training
Share production's ArcGIS Data Store so testers use live data
questions.explanation: Esri describes staging as a representative mirror of production: it typically reflects the same tiers, servers, components and roles, but a scaled-down deployment may be acceptable to reduce cost. An identical clone is not required and is described as costly.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Environment isolation

questions.objective: Design system based on environment isolation needs
questions.question: A developer has finished an Experience Builder app that references a web map and several feature layers held in a group in the development ArcGIS Enterprise deployment. The team wants a repeatable way to move these items into the separate staging deployment for review. What does Esri recommend?
answers: Use Export Group Content and Import Group Content, scriptable with GroupMigrationManager
Create a distributed collaboration between development and staging and share the group to the collaboration workspace
Run the WebGISDR tool to export the development deployment and import the backup file into the staging deployment
Recreate each item by hand in staging from its JSON in development
questions.explanation: Esri's environment isolation guidance describes exporting group content to a package, adding it to the target environment and importing it into a group, scriptable with GroupMigrationManager in the ArcGIS API for Python. WebGISDR restores an entire deployment and would overwrite staging rather than promote selected content.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Environment isolation
source.section: Working with multiple ArcGIS Enterprise deployments

questions.objective: Design system based on environment isolation needs
questions.question: An organisation must upgrade ArcGIS Enterprise with almost no disruption to production users and is willing to run two full environments for a period. Which approach fits this requirement?
answers: Blue-green: upgrade and test the idle environment, then switch traffic at the load balancer
An in-place upgrade of production during business hours, followed by testing in the development environment
A WebGISDR backup of production, restored onto a staging environment that then becomes a read-only replica
A distributed collaboration that copies all production content to the upgraded deployment before cut-over
questions.explanation: In a blue-green deployment, two identical environments take turns as production; the upgrade is done on the idle one and, once tested, only the direction of traffic from the proxy or load balancer changes. The Architecture Center notes cloud infrastructure makes this more affordable.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Environment isolation

questions.objective: Determine which type of collaboration to use based on requirements
questions.question: A city's public works team uses an ArcGIS Online organisation, and two other departments each run their own ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 deployment. They want to set up a single distributed collaboration that includes all three. Which participant must be the collaboration host?
answers: The ArcGIS Online organisation, because it must host any collaboration that includes ArcGIS Online
Whichever ArcGIS Enterprise deployment holds the authoritative data, with ArcGIS Online joining as a guest
Either participant, provided all ArcGIS Enterprise guests are at the same version as the host
Neither; ArcGIS Online can only collaborate with ArcGIS Enterprise through a partnered collaboration
questions.explanation: When a collaboration includes an ArcGIS Online organisation, ArcGIS Online must always be the host, and the ArcGIS Enterprise participants (10.5.1 or later) join as guests.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Set up an ArcGIS Enterprise and ArcGIS Online collaboration

questions.objective: Determine which type of collaboration to use based on requirements
questions.question: Field crews use ArcGIS Field Maps against ArcGIS Online, often offline. Authoritative hosted feature layers live in ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4, and field edits must flow back to Enterprise. The layers meet all sync and replica-tracking prerequisites. How should the collaboration be configured?
answers: Share the layers as copies with two-way edits enabled, with the Enterprise guest given Send and Receive access
Share the layers by reference, with the Enterprise guest given Send access so edits are written back to the source
Share the layers as copies with one-way edits, with the Enterprise guest given Receive access to the workspace
Share the layers by reference with Send and Receive access, and enable offline mode on the referenced items
questions.explanation: Two-way editing requires the workspace to share feature layers as copies and both the configuring and receiving participants to have Send and Receive access. Layers shared by reference are not copied, so offline edits in ArcGIS Online cannot synchronise back through the collaboration.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Share content with collaboration groups
source.section: Edits made by owner and receiver (two-way)

questions.objective: Determine which type of collaboration to use based on requirements
questions.question: An agency wants its on-premises ArcGIS Enterprise deployment to join an ArcGIS Online-hosted collaboration. The security team will not allow any inbound connections from the internet to the portal. What is the network requirement?
answers: Allow outbound HTTPS on port 443, because the Enterprise portal initiates all communication
Allow inbound HTTPS on port 443 to the portal, because ArcGIS Online pushes shared content to each guest
Allow inbound traffic on port 7443 to the portal, because ArcGIS Online calls the portal administrator API
Set up a site-to-site VPN to Esri for all collaboration traffic
questions.explanation: In an ArcGIS Enterprise and ArcGIS Online collaboration, all communication is initiated by the ArcGIS Enterprise portal, so firewall rules need to allow outbound communication over port 443. No inbound access from ArcGIS Online is required.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Set up an ArcGIS Enterprise and ArcGIS Online collaboration

questions.objective: Determine which type of collaboration to use based on requirements
questions.question: A collaboration workspace is configured to share feature layers as copies with two-way edits. A participant shares a sync-enabled feature service that runs on traditionally versioned data (without the move-edits-to-base option). What will recipients receive?
answers: A copy of the layer that supports one-way edits only, because traditional versioning cannot do bidirectional sync
A copy of the layer that supports two-way edits, because the workspace setting overrides the data's versioning type
A reference to the source layer, because traditionally versioned data can never be shared as a copy
Nothing, because the service fails the two-way prerequisites and the workspace blocks the share entirely
questions.explanation: Feature services on traditionally versioned data do not support bidirectional sync, so they can be shared one-way only. If a service has sync enabled but does not meet the two-way requirements, it is shared as a copy with one-way editing, even if the workspace is set up for two-way edits.

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to identify a content delivery strategy
questions.question: A government agency serves internal analysts and decision makers through ArcGIS Enterprise. It now needs to publish information maps to the general public and is concerned about improper access to internal content and the effect of public traffic on its infrastructure. What strategy does Esri recommend?
answers: Serve public users from a separate ArcGIS Enterprise deployment or from ArcGIS Online
Share the public maps with Everyone in the existing internal portal and add Web Adaptor instances for load
Expose the internal portal to the internet and rely on group sharing to keep internal content hidden
Create a public guest account in the internal portal with a custom role
questions.explanation: Esri recommends separating operational and transactional users from public information users with separate environments, using multiple ArcGIS Enterprise deployments or ArcGIS Online. This prevents improper access to internal content by external users and reduces the traffic impact on internal infrastructure.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Best practices for system architecture

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to identify a content delivery strategy
questions.question: An organisation plans to place a third-party content delivery network (CDN) in front of web apps hosted in its internet-facing ArcGIS Enterprise deployment. Which approach follows Esri guidance?
answers: Cache static HTML, CSS and JavaScript, not dynamic REST responses, and invalidate on upgrade
Cache all REST API responses, including feature queries, for 24 hours to minimise load on ArcGIS Server
Cache only portal sign-in and token responses so that authentication remains fast for distant users
Cache everything at the CDN edge and never invalidate it, because ArcGIS Enterprise versions its URLs
questions.explanation: The Architecture Center advises distinguishing static assets suitable for CDN caching from dynamic REST API responses that should not be cached, and forcibly invalidating the CDN cache when ArcGIS Enterprise is upgraded or an app changes.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Optimize performance in ArcGIS

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to identify a content delivery strategy
questions.question: A public-facing app needs a fast, highly scalable reference layer built from data updated a few times a year. Users must switch between light and dark cartographic styles and toggle labels on the same layer. Which delivery option best meets these needs?
answers: A vector tile layer, with alternative styles applied on the client to the same tile set
A cached map image layer, generating a separate raster cache for each style and label combination
A dynamic map image layer, drawing each request on the server from the source data
A hosted feature layer with query response caching enabled, styled in each user's browser
questions.explanation: Vector tiles are rendered on the client using a separate style, so a single tile set can show multiple cartographic versions and hide or show layers. Raster tiles offer one fixed cartographic representation and cannot be restyled or have labels turned off.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Optimize performance in ArcGIS

questions.objective: Identify methods for backup, replication and/or resiliency
questions.question: An administrator uses the WebGISDR tool to replicate a primary ArcGIS Enterprise deployment to a disconnected standby. Services reference an enterprise geodatabase registered with the federated server, and several map services are cached. What must the administrator replicate separately from WebGISDR?
answers: Registered enterprise geodatabase data and map service cache tiles
The hosted feature layer data held in the ArcGIS Data Store relational data store
Portal items, users, groups and sharing settings
The federated and hosting ArcGIS Server site settings and their published services
questions.explanation: WebGISDR captures portal content, federated server settings and relational and tile cache data store content, but it does not copy data from databases or folders registered with ArcGIS Server, and it does not move map service cache tiles. The administrator must replicate those separately.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Disaster recovery and replication

questions.objective: Identify methods for backup, replication and/or resiliency
questions.question: Stakeholders tell an architect: 'We can lose at most two hours of edits, and the system must be usable again within eight hours of a disaster.' Which statement correctly applies these requirements?
