answers: Two hours is the RPO and drives backup frequency; eight hours is the RTO
The two-hour figure is the RTO and drives backup frequency; the eight-hour figure is the RPO for restoring
Both figures are RTOs, so the architect needs a hot standby kept running at full capacity at all times
Both are RPOs, so a full backup every two hours is all that is needed
questions.explanation: The Recovery Point Objective is how much data can be lost and relates to the type and frequency of backups; the Recovery Time Objective is how long until the system is back up. Here the RPO is two hours and the RTO is eight hours.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Backups and disaster recovery

questions.objective: Identify methods for backup, replication and/or resiliency
questions.question: An IT team proposes using hypervisor snapshots of the running Portal for ArcGIS and ArcGIS Data Store VMs as the only backup in the organisation's BC/DR plan. What is Esri's guidance?
answers: They are not durable BC/DR backups; if used, take them with ArcGIS Enterprise services stopped
Snapshots are the preferred DR method because they integrate with the portal and data store databases
Snapshots are acceptable only if they are taken during peak hours, so they capture the latest edits
Snapshots can replace WebGISDR, provided the file share for the portal content directory is excluded
questions.explanation: Esri states VM snapshots are useful for low RTO but are not considered durable backups in a broader BC/DR plan. Because the portal and data store databases do not integrate with these tools, snapshots should be taken after stopping the running ArcGIS Enterprise components.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Back up and restore best practices

questions.objective: Identify methods for backup, replication and/or resiliency
questions.question: An organisation is designing a geographically redundant ArcGIS Enterprise deployment with a standby in a second data centre, kept current using WebGISDR. Which design choice meets Esri's requirements?
answers: Keep identical organisation URLs at both sites and repoint them via global DNS on failover
Run the standby on Linux to reduce cost while the primary runs on Windows, using the same software version
Deploy the standby one release ahead to speed up the next upgrade
Give the standby fewer machines and its own hostnames, then update item URLs in the portal after failover
questions.explanation: Geographic redundancy requires duplicated environments with the same number of machines and the same component URLs; failover is typically done by reassigning host names through a global site selector or global DNS. Both sites must also use the same operating system and software version.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Disaster recovery and replication

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine when to use tiered architectures
questions.question: A small team runs ArcGIS Enterprise on a single machine. Usage is now growing fast: many more users, a large number of portal items and heavy editing of hosted layers. How does Esri suggest the deployment should evolve?
answers: Put Portal for ArcGIS and ArcGIS Data Store on separate machines from each other and GIS Server
Keep all components on one machine but add CPU and memory, since a single machine is simplest to replicate
Move ArcGIS Data Store onto the Portal for ArcGIS machine and dedicate the original machine to Web Adaptor
Replace the hosting server with a federated server so that the portal no longer stores hosted layer data
questions.explanation: Esri states that a lightly used deployment can run on one machine, but a heavily used deployment (many users, many items or heavy editing) should install Portal for ArcGIS and ArcGIS Data Store on machines separate from each other and from the GIS Server machines.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Disaster recovery and replication

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine when to use tiered architectures
questions.question: To improve resilience, an architect proposes placing the portal and hosting server tiers in one data centre and the ArcGIS Data Store tier and the registered enterprise geodatabase in a second data centre 300 km away. What is the most appropriate response?
answers: Keep all tiers of one deployment in one data centre; add a secondary deployment for DR
Accept the design, provided the link between data centres has enough bandwidth for peak data store traffic
Accept it, but move only the geodatabase back beside the hosting server
Split each tier across both data centres instead, so every tier has a primary and standby at different sites
questions.explanation: ArcGIS Enterprise components for one deployment, including each data store type, must be in a single data centre or equivalent, and services should be in the same data centre as their data. To guard against data centre loss, Esri recommends a secondary deployment in a separate data centre.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 system requirements

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine when to use tiered architectures
questions.question: An organisation must make services from its internal ArcGIS Server site available to internet users without exposing the internal machines directly. Which tiered design follows Esri guidance?
answers: Put a reverse proxy in the perimeter network that forwards HTTPS requests to Web Adaptor or ArcGIS Server inside
Move the ArcGIS Server machines into the perimeter network and keep only the database tier in the internal network
Put a reverse proxy in the perimeter network that terminates TLS and forwards plain HTTP to ArcGIS Server
Open port 6443 on the external firewall so internet clients connect straight to the ArcGIS Server machines
questions.explanation: Esri describes a reverse proxy deployed in a perimeter network (DMZ) that forwards internet requests to machines in the internal network, masking their identity. ArcGIS Server does not support SSL offloading, so the proxy must forward to Web Adaptor or ArcGIS Server over HTTPS.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 documentation: Configure a reverse proxy server with ArcGIS Server

bundles.title: Bundle 5: Physical Architecture (scenarios)
bundles.description: Scenario-based questions on documenting, sizing, adjusting and making highly available the physical architecture of ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4, including URLs and ArcGIS Pro VDI choices.

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to document physical architecture that will meet nonfunctional requirements
questions.question: A project sponsor accepts that the new ArcGIS Enterprise deployment needs a staging environment for upgrade and patch testing, but rejects the budget for a full copy of the production hardware. The GIS manager worries that anything less will make staging tests meaningless. How should you document the staging environment?
answers: Mirror production's tiers, components and roles, but allow smaller machine capacity than production
Drop staging and test patches in production during a scheduled out-of-hours maintenance window
Use the development environment for patch testing so that only two environments need to be funded
Deploy staging as a single-machine base deployment even though production uses multiple machines
questions.explanation: Esri describes staging as a representative mirror of production: it reflects production's tiers, servers, components and roles, but may not need the same per-server capacity, so a scaled-down deployment can save cost. Collapsing staging onto one machine loses the representativeness that makes the testing valid.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Environment isolation

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to document physical architecture that will meet nonfunctional requirements
questions.question: During requirements workshops, the operations manager states: "If we lose the data centre, we can accept re-capturing up to 4 hours of field edits, and the system must be usable again within 24 hours." How should you record these nonfunctional requirements in the physical architecture document?
answers: An RPO of 4 hours and an RTO of 24 hours, so backups or replication must run at least every 4 hours
An RTO of 4 hours and an RPO of 24 hours, so a full system rebuild must finish within 4 hours
A 99.9% uptime SLA, which the 4-hour and 24-hour figures together convert into for the year
A high-availability requirement, so primary and standby machines are placed in separate data centres
questions.explanation: The Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is how much data loss, expressed in time, is acceptable; the Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is how long until the system is available again. Swapping the two terms is the common error, and HA components should not be split across data centres anyway.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Backups and disaster recovery

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to document physical architecture that will meet nonfunctional requirements
questions.question: The infrastructure team proposes that its existing hourly hypervisor snapshots of every ArcGIS Enterprise VM, taken throughout the working day, will be the only disaster recovery mechanism. The GIS manager is concerned about edits and publishing in progress when a snapshot runs. What is the most appropriate recommendation?
answers: Use the WebGISDR tool for application-consistent DR backups, and keep any VM snapshots to off-peak times
Accept the snapshots as they are, because a VM-level backup captures every component in a consistent state
Replace the snapshots with portal, server and data store backups, which Esri intends as the primary DR method
Rely on a highly available deployment instead, because HA removes the need for a separate DR approach
questions.explanation: VM snapshots operate below the application and do not guarantee application consistency, for example during publishing or edits; Esri recommends the WebGISDR tool for DR and suggests off-peak timing for snapshots. Single-component backups are intended for restore in place, not DR.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Backups and disaster recovery

questions.objective: Design a highly available deployment
questions.question: To shorten the monthly maintenance window, the operations team plans to install the latest ArcGIS Enterprise patches on both portal machines, all hosting server machines and both data store machines at the same time on Saturday night. The deployment is configured for high availability. What should you advise?
answers: Patch the machines in each tier one at a time so at least one machine per tier stays available
Patch all machines together, because HA components automatically defer updates until failover completes
Patch the standby machines in every tier together first, then patch all primary machines together
Take WebGISDR backups first, then patch all machines together, since the backup removes any risk
questions.explanation: Esri states that you should not patch both portal machines, all server machines or both data store machines at the same time; patch them one at a time so each tier always has availability. Patching everything together, even after a backup, removes the redundancy HA is meant to provide.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Apply patches and updates to highly available components

questions.objective: Design a highly available deployment
questions.question: An administrator stopped and patched the primary relational ArcGIS Data Store machine in a highly available deployment. Hosted feature layers stopped working for the duration, even though the standby machine was healthy. What procedure should be used next time?
answers: Patch the standby, promote it with makePrimary, then patch the former primary once it is the standby
Patch the primary as before, but first shorten the failover monitoring interval so the standby takes over
Patch both data store machines at once, because a stopped primary forces an immediate failover
Unregister the standby before patching the primary, then re-register it once the patch is applied
questions.explanation: By default ArcGIS Data Store does not fail over when the service is stopped, so patching the primary first takes hosted services offline. Esri's procedure is to patch the standby, use makePrimary to promote it, then patch the former primary.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Apply patches and updates to highly available components
source.section: Apply patches to a highly available ArcGIS Data Store

questions.objective: Design a highly available deployment
questions.question: A design for an on-premises, highly available ArcGIS Enterprise deployment has two portal machines, a three-machine hosting server site and a primary/standby relational data store. The portal content directory, server directories and configuration store all sit on a share hosted by a single Windows file server VM. What is the key issue to raise?
answers: The single file server is a single point of failure; host the shares on highly available storage such as a NAS or RAID
The content directory must be stored locally on each portal machine, with one copy kept on every portal machine
The configuration store must be moved into the relational data store so that it fails over automatically
The design is acceptable, because ArcGIS Server caches its configuration store in memory on every machine
questions.explanation: Portal for ArcGIS and ArcGIS Server both rely on shared storage for HA, so that storage can itself be a single point of failure; on-premises, Esri recommends a NAS device or RAID to make it highly available. The portal content directory must be shared, not local.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: High availability in ArcGIS Enterprise
source.section: Storage for configuration files and data

questions.objective: Design a highly available deployment
questions.question: A highly available portal sits behind a load balancer that forwards port 443 traffic to an ArcGIS Web Adaptor (IIS) in front of each portal machine. After the team enables Integrated Windows Authentication at the web tier, the load balancer marks both targets unhealthy and the portal becomes unreachable. What change should be made?
answers: Update the load balancer health check to expect a 401 response from the web adaptor instead of a 200
Remove the health check from the load balancer and fall back to plain round-robin across both targets
Point the load balancer health check at port 7443 on the standby portal machine only, not the primary
Disable web-tier authentication again, because a highly available portal does not support web-tier IWA
questions.explanation: When web-tier authentication is used, Esri instructs you to update the health check URL to expect a 401 response from ArcGIS Web Adaptor instead of a 200. Removing health checks would leave the load balancer unable to detect a failed portal machine.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Configure a highly available portal
source.section: Install and configure the first ArcGIS Web Adaptor

questions.objective: Design a highly available deployment
questions.question: A council's highly available ArcGIS Enterprise deployment suffered a full outage. Investigation showed the standby portal machine had failed three weeks earlier, and nobody noticed because users saw no disruption. When the primary failed, nothing was left. What should be added to the architecture?
answers: Monitoring and alerting on each machine, for example ArcGIS Monitor, so a failed node is fixed promptly
A third portal machine, so the deployment can survive two failures without any administrator involvement
Shorter portal failover settings, so the standby is promoted faster when the primary becomes unavailable
Nightly WebGISDR backups, since these alert administrators whenever any highly available machine fails
questions.explanation: Once one machine in an HA component fails, the deployment has a single point of failure; Esri says machines must be monitored, with ArcGIS Monitor or third-party software, so administrators are notified. Adding more portal machines does not help, because a highly available portal is configured with two machines, and backups do not raise alerts.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: High availability in ArcGIS Enterprise

questions.objective: Identify the URLs used in ArcGIS Enterprise
questions.question: An external reverse proxy forwards https://maps.example.com/server to an internal ArcGIS Web Adaptor. External users can open the Services Directory, but links in it point to https://gisweb01.internal.example.com/server/..., which fails with a 404 outside the network. What is the most likely fix?
answers: Configure the reverse proxy to pass the X-Forwarded-Host header with the original host name
Add the internal host name to the public DNS zone so external clients can resolve the links
Enable HTTP on port 6080 so the reverse proxy can rewrite the links in the HTML responses
Rename the web adaptor to arcgis so that it matches the default ArcGIS Server site name
questions.explanation: ArcGIS Server and ArcGIS Web Adaptor expect the X-Forwarded-Host header from the reverse proxy; without it they may return the internal machine URL, which clients cannot reach and which exposes internal details. Publishing internal names in public DNS would only worsen that exposure.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Configure a reverse proxy server with ArcGIS Server

questions.objective: Identify the URLs used in ArcGIS Enterprise
questions.question: The web team wants the new highly available portal, fronted by a third-party load balancer without ArcGIS Web Adaptor, to be reached at https://www.example.com/departments/gis/portal so it fits the corporate site structure. What is the most appropriate response?
answers: Explain that the context must be one level deep and propose a URL such as https://gis.example.com/portal
Accept the URL and set WebContextURL to the full path so the portal builds the correct item links
Accept the URL, but add a second load balancer to strip the /departments/gis segment from requests
Accept the URL, provided that HTTPS is terminated at the load balancer and HTTP is used to the portal
questions.explanation: Esri requires the load balancer context name to be only one level deep: https://lb.example.com/enterprise is allowed, but https://lb.example.com/myorg/enterprise is not. TLS termination is not a workaround and is itself unsupported for Portal for ArcGIS.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Configure a highly available portal
source.section: Prerequisites to configure a highly available portal

questions.objective: Identify the URLs used in ArcGIS Enterprise
questions.question: IT security has disabled administrative access through ArcGIS Web Adaptor on a stand-alone ArcGIS Server site published at https://gis.example.com/server. A GIS analyst on the internal network needs to make an administrator connection from ArcGIS Pro to register a database. Which URL should the analyst use?
answers: https://gisserver.example.com:6443/arcgis
https://gis.example.com/server/admin
https://gis.example.com/server/manager
https://gisserver.example.com:7443/arcgis
questions.explanation: When administrative access through the web adaptor is disabled, an ArcGIS Server administrator connection uses the machine URL with the port, such as https://gisserver.domain.com:6443/arcgis. Port 7443 belongs to Portal for ArcGIS, not ArcGIS Server.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Components of ArcGIS URLs
source.section: ArcGIS Server administrator and publisher connections

questions.objective: Given a scenario, use system design inputs to calculate required server capacities
questions.question: You are planning a replicated disaster recovery deployment using the webgisdr utility. The primary deployment has a two-machine GIS Server hosting site, Portal for ArcGIS on its own machine, and ArcGIS Data Store on two machines (a relational data store and a tile cache data store on separate machines). Using Esri's formula, how many machines are needed in total across primary and standby?
questions.explanation: Esri's formula is (number of GIS Server machines + 1 Portal for ArcGIS machine + number of data store machines) x 2, so (2 + 1 + 2) x 2 = 10. Five counts only the primary, and the data centres should match to avoid performance issues after failover.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Disaster recovery and replication

questions.objective: Given a scenario, use system design inputs to calculate required server capacities
questions.question: Load testing shows that, at peak, a hosting server site needs a total of 24 vCPUs of ArcGIS Server capacity to meet response-time targets. The design uses a three-machine site for high availability, and the SLA requires performance to hold if any one machine fails. How many vCPUs should each machine have, at minimum?
questions.explanation: If one machine fails, the system's capacity drops, so Esri says to build extra capacity into each machine so the remaining machines can handle the load. With three machines, the two survivors must carry 24 vCPUs, so each needs 12. Eight per machine meets peak only when all three are running.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Configure highly available ArcGIS Enterprise

questions.objective: Given a scenario, use system design inputs to calculate required server capacities
questions.question: A spatiotemporal big data store machine has a 2 TB data disk. The administrator is preparing to upgrade ArcGIS Data Store. According to the ArcGIS Data Store system requirements, how much disk space on that machine must be free for temporary files during the upgrade?
answers: At least 400 GB
At least 200 GB
At least 13 GB
At least 10 GB
questions.explanation: A minimum of 20 percent of the disk space on each machine must be available for temporary files when configuring or upgrading a spatiotemporal big data store; 20% of 2 TB is 400 GB. The 13 GB figure is the minimum to install ArcGIS Data Store, and 10 GB is the low-disk warning threshold.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: ArcGIS Data Store system requirements

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to adjust architecture to meet requirements and constraints
questions.question: A highly available portal uses built-in users and must be reachable from the internet through a load balancer in the DMZ. IT security will not open ports 6443 or 7443 from that DMZ load balancer to the internal network, but the portal and hosting server must still talk to each other with redundancy. What should you do?
answers: Add an internal load balancer for the Administration URL (port 6443) and privatePortalURL (port 7443)
Set the privatePortalURL to the primary portal machine's URL so the servers avoid the DMZ load balancer
Ask IT security for an exception, because ArcGIS Enterprise HA cannot work without these DMZ ports
Federate the hosting server using one server machine's URL as the Administration URL to avoid the DMZ
questions.explanation: Esri's scenario places a second, internal load balancer inside the firewall so the portal reaches the hosting server through the Administration URL and the servers reach the portal through the privatePortalURL without crossing the firewall. Pointing either URL at a single machine breaks redundancy.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Highly available ArcGIS Enterprise deployment scenarios
source.section: Built-in users and clients have access to the portal

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to adjust architecture to meet requirements and constraints
questions.question: To reduce load on the backend VMs, the network team wants the load balancer to terminate TLS and forward plain HTTP to Portal for ArcGIS and ArcGIS Server. The GIS manager wants to keep the load balancer. What is the most appropriate response?
answers: Keep the load balancer, but re-encrypt traffic to the backends so that TLS is maintained end to end
Accept the proposal, but enable HTTP on ports 7080 and 6080 on all of the portal and server machines
Accept the proposal for Portal for ArcGIS only, and keep HTTPS for the ArcGIS Server machines only
Remove the load balancer and expose ports 7443 and 6443 directly so clients connect over HTTPS
questions.explanation: Esri states that TLS termination is generally not recommended for ArcGIS and is not supported for Portal for ArcGIS; end-to-end TLS is the stronger posture. Removing the load balancer would expose backend ports and lose the single point of entry.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Load balancers and reverse proxies

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to adjust architecture to meet requirements and constraints
questions.question: The network team moves the relational ArcGIS Data Store machine into a separate secured subnet and opens only port 2443 from the hosting server site. The data store validates, but hosted feature layers fail when they are published or queried. Which additional port should be opened between the hosting server machines and the relational data store?
answers: 9220 (HTTPS)
7443 (HTTPS)
questions.explanation: Port 2443 carries configuration and machine communication, but internal communication between the hosting server and the relational data store uses port 9876. Ports 29080 and 9220 serve the tile cache and spatiotemporal big data stores respectively.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Ports used by ArcGIS Data Store

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to adjust architecture to meet requirements and constraints
questions.question: An analysis team regularly runs long geoprocessing services on the single ArcGIS Server site that also serves the council's busy public map services, and map response times degrade during those jobs. The budget covers one additional VM. Which change best addresses the requirement?
answers: Use the VM for a separate ArcGIS Server site dedicated to geoprocessing, and route those requests to it
Join the VM to the existing site so the geoprocessing and map workloads share a larger compute pool
Use the VM as a second web adaptor so incoming requests are spread across two web servers instead
Use the VM for a standby portal, because portal capacity limits geoprocessing job submission speed
questions.explanation: Esri recommends workload separation through multiple ArcGIS Server sites, for example one site for geoprocessing and another for map services, so a large geoprocessing task does not affect map services. Adding the machine to the same site still lets the two workloads compete for the same resources.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Best practices for system architecture

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine which VDI configuration to use
questions.question: An on-premises VMware Horizon deployment gives ArcGIS Pro users vGPU-enabled virtual desktops. 3D scene navigation is choppy, and the VDI team finds the Horizon clients are connecting with RDP. Server-side GPU and CPU utilisation are moderate. What is the most appropriate change?
answers: Configure the Horizon clients to connect with Blast Extreme or PCoIP instead of RDP
Increase each desktop's vCPU count, because ArcGIS Pro renders 3D scenes on the CPU
Move the users to RDSH sessions so that one host GPU is shared by all user sessions
Switch ArcGIS Pro to OpenGL rendering, because DirectX is not supported in Horizon
questions.explanation: Esri notes that the Horizon client can use RDP, PCoIP or Blast Extreme, but PCoIP and Blast are recommended for ArcGIS Pro and 3D rendering. RDSH lacks a hypervisor-level vGPU manager and is not designed for 3D applications.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro 3.4: VMware Horizon View on-premises VDI
source.section: 5. Create and configure the virtual machines

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine which VDI configuration to use
questions.question: A cloud team plans to deliver ArcGIS Pro through Azure Virtual Desktop by publishing it as an application on a few large multisession VMs, packing as many concurrent users onto each VM as possible to minimise cost. Which configuration best aligns with Esri guidance?
answers: Use supported N-series VMs with full desktops, or limit the number of connections per VM if Pro is published as an app
Keep the plan as proposed, because Azure Virtual Desktop shares the GPU fairly across any number of sessions
Use general-purpose VMs without GPUs, because Azure Virtual Desktop emulates a GPU for each user session
Publish Pro through Citrix Virtual Apps on the same VMs, because it manages GPU memory between sessions
questions.explanation: For Azure Virtual Desktop, Esri recommends supported N-series VMs on a full Windows VM desktop, and when ArcGIS Pro is published as an application, a limited number of connections per Windows VM. Citrix Virtual Apps is not recommended or supported for ArcGIS Pro.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro 3.4: ArcGIS Pro 3.4 system requirements

bundles.title: Bundle 6: Solution Architecture (scenarios)
bundles.description: Scenario-based questions on choosing ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 components, server roles, data stores and authentication, and adapting designs to security, network and budget constraints.

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS components that will be required in the design
questions.question: A council's security standard requires all inbound web traffic to pass through its WAF-enabled reverse proxy, which the network team fully owns and supports. Staff will sign in with SAML, so no web-tier authentication is needed, and the web team does not want to run IIS or Tomcat for ArcGIS. What is the most appropriate design for the ArcGIS Enterprise web tier?
answers: Route the reverse proxy directly to Portal for ArcGIS and ArcGIS Server over HTTPS, meeting Esri's context, header and WebContextURL requirements
Install ArcGIS Web Adaptor on IIS anyway, because every ArcGIS Enterprise deployment must include it, whatever the authentication method chosen
Terminate TLS on the reverse proxy and forward plain HTTP to ports 7080 and 6080 to reduce certificate management on the ArcGIS machines
Publish ports 7443 and 6443 through the firewall alongside the reverse proxy so that clients can fall back to them if the proxy fails
questions.explanation: Esri describes ArcGIS Web Adaptor as recommended but optional unless web-tier authentication is required, and a third-party reverse proxy can route directly to the components over HTTPS if Esri requirements are met. SSL offloading is not supported, and internal component ports should never be exposed directly to clients.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: ArcGIS Web Adaptor and alternatives

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS components that will be required in the design
questions.question: A water utility's ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 portal has one federated ArcGIS GIS Server site that publishes map services from its enterprise geodatabase, but no hosting server. The operations manager now wants to dispatch crews with ArcGIS Workforce. The DBA suggests simply pointing Workforce at the enterprise geodatabase. What should the architect add?
answers: A hosting server with an ArcGIS Data Store relational data store, because Workforce relies on the relational data store
A spatiotemporal big data store registered with the federated site, because Workforce stores worker locations there
A new feature dataset in the enterprise geodatabase, registered with the federated site as the data store for Workforce projects
An ArcGIS Data Store object store on its own machine, because Workforce projects are stored as hosted 3D tiles layers
questions.explanation: Esri lists ArcGIS Workforce, with ArcGIS Insights and the Workflow Manager web app, among apps that rely on the relational data store, which is configured with the portal's hosting server. Registering the enterprise geodatabase does not provide the hosted feature layers these apps create.

source.title: Portal for ArcGIS 11.4: Apps and functionality that require ArcGIS Data Store

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS components that will be required in the design
questions.question: An agency is building an ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 deployment on a network with no internet access. Field teams want to design forms and view results on the ArcGIS Survey123 website as they would in a connected organisation. What should the architect add to the design?
answers: Install the Survey123 website from the installer on My Esri, on the portal machine or a stand-alone web server
Allow outbound access from the portal to survey123.arcgis.com, since the website cannot be hosted inside the network
Tell field teams that Survey123 is unavailable in disconnected deployments and that Field Maps forms must be used instead
Deploy a federated ArcGIS Notebook Server site, which hosts the Survey123 website and its REST API inside a container
questions.explanation: Esri documents a Survey123 website installer, downloaded from My Esri, that hosts the website and Survey123 REST API locally in a disconnected environment, on the portal machine or a separate web server. Opening access to the internet-hosted site would breach the disconnected requirement and is not needed.

source.title: Portal for ArcGIS 11.4: Configure a disconnected deployment

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS Server roles/extensions that will be required in the design
questions.question: An asset management team wants ArcGIS Workflow Manager to coordinate field and office jobs. The project sponsor has approved the server role licence but will not fund another virtual machine this financial year. The base deployment has a single hosting server machine with spare capacity. What is the most appropriate design?
answers: Install ArcGIS Workflow Manager Server on the hosting server machine and federate it with the portal, as Esri documents
Defer the project, because ArcGIS Workflow Manager Server must always run on a dedicated three-machine site of its own in production
Install ArcGIS Workflow Manager Server on the relational data store machine so that it sits next to the workflow data
Enable Workflow Manager as a capability on the existing hosting server's map services instead of adding a server role
questions.explanation: Esri states that ArcGIS Workflow Manager Server can be installed on its own machine or on the same machine as the hosting server, with its own Web Adaptor, and federated with the portal. Placing it on the data store machine conflicts with the guidance to keep ArcGIS Data Store machines separate.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: ArcGIS Enterprise server roles

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS Server roles/extensions that will be required in the design
questions.question: A drone programme will use ArcGIS Video Server 11.4. The pilots need several output resolutions for each video and record some footage in codecs other than H.264 or H.265. To save costs, the infrastructure team proposes standard virtual machines without GPUs. What is the most appropriate response?
answers: Specify an NVIDIA GPU with NVENC/NVDEC, because without one you cannot choose output resolutions or publish those other codecs
Accept the proposal, because Video Server transcodes every supported codec on the CPU with no loss of publishing options
Advise that Video Server will not install at all without a GPU, so the project cannot proceed on the standard virtual machines proposed
Add more CPU cores and RAM to the virtual machines, which Esri recommends as the equivalent of a GPU for video transcoding
questions.explanation: Video Server can be installed without a GPU, but it then cannot offer output resolutions when publishing, cannot publish files encoded with codecs other than H.264 and H.265, and streaming performance suffers. Esri recommends NVIDIA GPUs that support NVENC and NVDEC.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: ArcGIS Video Server 11.4 system requirements

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS Server roles/extensions that will be required in the design
questions.question: An ArcGIS Knowledge Server 11.4 site holds a knowledge graph of public infrastructure projects. The communications manager asks for it to be shared with everyone so that anonymous visitors to the public website can explore it. What should the architect advise?
answers: Knowledge graphs can be shared only with signed-in organisation members, so public access needs a different publishing approach
Enable anonymous access on the Knowledge Server site's Web Adaptor and then share the knowledge graph with Everyone
Federate the Knowledge Server site with a second, public-facing portal, where knowledge graphs can be shared with Everyone
Move the knowledge graph to a NoSQL data store, because only hosted graphs in the graph store are restricted from public sharing
questions.explanation: Esri states that all users must be signed in to the portal organisation to access a knowledge graph, and a knowledge graph cannot be shared with everyone, only with organisation members. Changing Web Adaptor or federation settings does not lift this restriction.

source.title: ArcGIS Knowledge 11.4: Configure ArcGIS Knowledge
source.section: Configure user privileges on the ArcGIS Enterprise portal

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS Server roles/extensions that will be required in the design
questions.question: In an ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 deployment, both the environmental science division and the land information division want their own ArcGIS Image Server site configured for raster analytics so their jobs do not compete. What should the architect recommend?
answers: Use one raster analytics Image Server site, as only one is allowed per deployment, and scale it with more RAM or machines
Federate two Image Server sites and set both as raster analytics servers, one for each division, on the same portal
Configure raster analytics on the hosting server for one division and on a federated Image Server site for the other
Deploy a GeoAnalytics Server site for the second division, as it provides the same raster analytics tools as Image Server
questions.explanation: Esri states that you can have only one ArcGIS Image Server site dedicated to raster analytics in an ArcGIS Enterprise deployment, and that it scales by adding RAM or machines. Additional Image Server sites can still be federated for dynamic image services.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: ArcGIS Enterprise server roles

questions.objective: Identify ArcGIS Server roles/extensions that will be required in the design
questions.question: A port authority will ingest three independent real-time feeds (vessel AIS, crane telemetry and gate sensors), each with moderate event volume and velocity, using ArcGIS GeoEvent Server. The infrastructure team proposes one multi-machine GeoEvent Server site behind ArcGIS Web Adaptor. Which design does Esri recommend?
answers: Several single-machine GeoEvent Server sites, each dedicated to specific data streams, without a Web Adaptor
One multi-machine GeoEvent Server site behind ArcGIS Web Adaptor, which balances the three feeds across machines
GeoEvent Server installed on each relational data store machine so that events are written locally as they arrive
One GeoEvent Server site federated as the hosting server, so all three feeds are stored in the relational data store
questions.explanation: For multiple data streams with moderate volume and velocity, Esri recommends multiple single-machine GeoEvent Server sites, each dedicated to specific streams. Esri also notes that GeoEvent Server sites are not configured with a Web Adaptor.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: ArcGIS Enterprise server roles

questions.objective: Identify appropriate Data Store types
questions.question: An intelligence unit's hosted knowledge graphs, created in an ArcGIS Data Store 11.4 graph store, are now business-critical. The GIS manager asks for the graph store to survive the loss of a machine. The infrastructure team proposes a three-machine cluster like the object store. What is the appropriate design?
answers: Add a second graph store machine as a standby; graph stores at 11.2 and later hold one or two machines in primary-standby mode
Build a three-machine graph store cluster, since graph stores replicate hosted knowledge graphs across an odd number of machines
Keep one graph store machine, because a graph store cannot have more than one machine and relies only on its backups
Move the hosted knowledge graphs into the relational data store, which already runs as a primary and standby pair
questions.explanation: Esri states that a graph store created with ArcGIS Data Store 11.2 or later can contain one or two machines, and a highly available graph store uses a primary and a standby to which hosted knowledge graphs are replicated. The one-machine limit applies only to legacy graph stores created at 11.1 or earlier, and cluster mode with three or more machines applies to the object store.

source.title: ArcGIS Data Store 11.4: Add machines to a data store

questions.objective: Identify appropriate Data Store types
questions.question: A design includes an ArcGIS Data Store object store for scene layers and 3D tiles. The project sponsor wants to start with one machine to save money and convert it to a cluster later if the 3D programme grows significantly. What should the architect advise?
answers: The mode cannot be changed later, so if growth is expected, create a cluster of at least three machines from the start
Start with one machine and add a second as a standby later, which converts the object store into a scalable cluster
Start with one machine and run the configuredatastore utility later to switch the existing object store to cluster mode
Start with a two-machine object store cluster, which is the minimum size that can later be extended with more machines
questions.explanation: An object store is either single-machine or cluster mode, and Esri states you cannot change modes after deploying; a cluster must contain at least three machines. The object store has no primary-standby option.

source.title: ArcGIS Data Store 11.4: Add machines to a data store

questions.objective: Identify appropriate Data Store types
questions.question: To support location sharing with high availability, an infrastructure team proposes a two-machine spatiotemporal big data store, reasoning that two machines work like a primary and standby pair. What should the architect recommend?
answers: Use an odd number of machines, such as three, because the spatiotemporal big data store always runs in cluster mode
Keep two machines and set one as standby, because the spatiotemporal big data store uses primary-standby replication
Use one machine with daily backups, because the spatiotemporal big data store does not support multiple machines
Keep two machines but give both only the data role, so that the coordinator role is handled by the hosting server
questions.explanation: The spatiotemporal big data store is always deployed in cluster mode, and Esri says to always use an odd number of machines, recommending three or five coordinator machines. Primary-standby mode applies to the relational data store and graph store, not this type.

source.title: ArcGIS Data Store 11.4: Add machines to a data store

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine authentication methods based on business needs
questions.question: A disconnected ArcGIS Enterprise deployment sits on a segmented network, and the portal machines have no route to the internet. Staff browsers can reach the organisation's cloud-hosted identity provider. The identity team suggests OpenID Connect because it is their newer standard. What should the architect recommend?
answers: Use SAML, loading the IdP metadata from a file, because SAML needs no runtime path from the portal to the IdP
Use OpenID Connect, because the browser exchanges the authorisation code for tokens without involving the portal
Use OpenID Connect with PKCE turned on, which removes the need for the portal to call the IdP token endpoint
Use SAML with the metadata URL option, so the portal re-polls the IdP for certificate changes automatically
questions.explanation: SAML is mediated by the browser, while OIDC requires the portal to call the IdP's token endpoint directly; a disconnected deployment with a cloud-hosted IdP is the one case OIDC cannot serve. Esri suggests a metadata file to avoid even the configuration-time fetch, and ArcGIS does not re-poll a metadata URL.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Authentication with SAML or OIDC
source.section: Key architectural difference: where the traffic goes

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine authentication methods based on business needs
questions.question: A regional emergency management portal must let staff from the host agency and from three partner agencies sign in with their own organisations' credentials. Each agency runs its own identity provider. The host agency's identity team prefers OpenID Connect. Which approach meets the requirement?
answers: SAML with a federation of identity providers, because ArcGIS supports only one OpenID Connect provider per organisation
OpenID Connect with one login per agency, because the portal supports a separate OIDC provider for each partner organisation
Integrated Windows Authentication across all agencies, configured through ArcGIS Web Adaptor (IIS) on the portal
A single direct SAML login for the host agency, with partner staff added as built-in accounts sharing one login
questions.explanation: Esri's decision guide recommends SAML with a federation of identity providers for multiple identity domains, because OIDC currently supports one provider per organisation. Shared built-in accounts would defeat named-user accountability.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Authentication with SAML or OIDC

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine authentication methods based on business needs
questions.question: An organisation will configure OpenID Connect logins for its highly available ArcGIS Enterprise portal, which has a standby portal and a disaster recovery replica. The network team asks which ArcGIS machines need firewall rules to reach the IdP's token, userinfo and JWKS endpoints. What should the architect tell them?
answers: Every portal machine, including standby and DR nodes; federated ArcGIS Server sites never contact the IdP
Only the active primary portal machine, because standby and DR nodes take over the existing login sessions
Every portal and federated ArcGIS Server machine, because each server validates the user's ID token itself
No ArcGIS machines, because with OpenID Connect only the user's browser communicates with the IdP endpoints
questions.explanation: Under OIDC the portal makes a back-channel call to the IdP, so every portal node, including standby and DR nodes, needs the network path and CA trust. Federated ArcGIS Server sites consume portal tokens and never contact the IdP.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Authentication with SAML or OIDC

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine authentication methods based on business needs
questions.question: Staff sign in to an ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 portal through a SAML identity provider. IT security now requires multi-factor authentication for every staff sign-in, and a GIS administrator suggests turning on the MFA setting in the portal. What is the most appropriate response?
answers: Have the identity team enforce MFA in the IdP's sign-in policy, as ArcGIS-native MFA applies only to built-in accounts
Turn on the portal's MFA setting, which adds a second sign-in prompt for SAML members after the IdP returns its assertion
Switch staff from SAML to built-in accounts so the portal's own MFA setting can be applied to every staff member
Enable encrypted SAML assertions, which Esri treats as meeting the requirement for a second authentication factor
questions.explanation: For SAML and OIDC members, MFA is entirely the IdP's responsibility; the ArcGIS-native MFA setting applies only to built-in accounts. Encrypted assertions protect the assertion's contents but are not a second factor.

source.title: ArcGIS Architecture Center: Authentication with SAML or OIDC

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine authentication methods based on business needs
questions.question: A portal uses SAML logins. The GIS manager wants access to restricted content controlled by IdP groups, so leavers and movers lose access without portal administrators editing groups by hand. The identity team confirms the IdP can send group claims. What should the architect specify?
answers: Enable SAML based group membership and link each portal group to the exact group value returned in the assertion
Configure an Active Directory group store in the portal's identity store alongside the SAML login for group lookups
Create portal groups whose names match the IdP group display names; the portal links them automatically by name
Turn on Update profiles on sign in, which refreshes each member's portal group membership from the IdP at sign-in
questions.explanation: With Enable SAML based group membership turned on, the portal parses the assertion for groups, and each portal group must reference the exact value returned in the SAML attribute. The Update profiles on sign in option refreshes only members' full names and email addresses.

source.title: Portal for ArcGIS 11.4: Configure a SAML-compliant identity provider with a portal
source.section: Configure the portal with a SAML identity provider

questions.objective: Given a scenario, determine authentication methods based on business needs
questions.question: A government agency issues smart cards and stores its users in an LDAP directory, not Active Directory. Its web tier runs Apache Tomcat. A security architect proposes ArcGIS Web Adaptor (IIS) for PKI client-certificate authentication to the portal. What should the architect specify?
answers: ArcGIS Web Adaptor (Java Platform) on the Java application server, configured for client certificates with an LDAP identity store
ArcGIS Web Adaptor (IIS) with Active Directory Client Certificate Mapping, pointed at the LDAP directory for user lookups
Portal-tier authentication against LDAP with anonymous access, and smart card checks enforced by the users' browsers
A SAML login with the portal acting as the identity provider itself, validating smart card certificates against the LDAP directory
questions.explanation: To use LDAP with PKI, Esri requires client certificate authentication through ArcGIS Web Adaptor (Java Platform) on a Java application server; ArcGIS Web Adaptor (IIS) cannot perform client certificate authentication with LDAP. IIS client certificate mapping applies to Windows Active Directory.

source.title: Portal for ArcGIS 11.4: Use LDAP and client certificate authentication to secure access
source.section: Configure ArcGIS Web Adaptor to use client certificate authentication

questions.objective: Adjust architectural solution to meet constraints
questions.question: A research agency's ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 deployment will run in a site with no internet connection. Users expect address search, printing from Map Viewer and directions to work as they do in the connected trial organisation. Which design change is required?
answers: Publish geocode, print and route services on ArcGIS Server and configure them as the portal's utility services
Ask IT security for a narrow firewall exception to the ArcGIS Online utility services used by Map Viewer
Accept that these functions are unavailable in disconnected deployments and remove them from the requirements
Install ArcGIS Pro on the portal machine so that Map Viewer can borrow its locator and print engine locally
questions.explanation: By default the portal uses ArcGIS Online for geocoding and printing and has no route service, so a disconnected deployment needs its own ArcGIS Server geocode, print and route services configured as utility services. A firewall exception would breach the no-internet constraint.

source.title: Portal for ArcGIS 11.4: Configure a disconnected deployment

questions.objective: Adjust architectural solution to meet constraints
questions.question: An agency is moving its ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 organisation to an isolated network. IT security will block every request to ArcGIS Online. Map authors currently rely on the Esri basemaps in the basemap gallery and want a basemap gallery that still works. What is the most appropriate response?
answers: Disable external content in the Portal Administrator Directory and point the basemap gallery at a group of custom basemaps
Ask IT security to allow basemap tile requests to ArcGIS Online only, since Esri basemaps are required by Map Viewer
Keep the default gallery and let ArcGIS Enterprise switch the Esri basemaps over to cached copies once the network is isolated
Download the Esri basemap items from Living Atlas into the portal before isolation, so the existing gallery keeps working
questions.explanation: Esri's preconfigured basemaps come from ArcGIS Online and are not supported in a disconnected environment; you disable external content and specify a custom group whose basemaps appear in the gallery. A firewall exception would breach the isolation requirement, and the portal does not cache the Esri basemaps automatically.

source.title: Portal for ArcGIS 11.4: Configure a disconnected deployment
source.section: Point the portal to local resources

questions.objective: Adjust architectural solution to meet constraints
questions.question: A stand-alone (non-federated) ArcGIS Server 11.4 site uses built-in users. IT security now wants access controlled by Active Directory groups, but the GIS team insists on keeping the existing built-in ArcGIS Server user accounts, so the proposal is to source only roles from Active Directory. What should the architect advise?
answers: Roles-only external stores are unsupported; source users from Active Directory, with roles there or in the built-in store
Accept the proposal, configuring the Active Directory store for roles only so built-in users can be mapped to AD groups
Accept the proposal, but deploy ArcGIS Web Adaptor (Java Platform) because it is required for AD-sourced role lookups
Federate the site with a portal first, because a stand-alone ArcGIS Server site cannot use any external identity store
questions.explanation: Esri states that an external identity store can manage both users and roles, or only users while the built-in store manages roles, but cannot manage only roles while the built-in store manages users. Stand-alone sites can use external identity stores, and Integrated Windows Authentication with Active Directory requires ArcGIS Web Adaptor (IIS), not the Java Platform version.

source.title: ArcGIS Server 11.4: Web-tier authentication

bundles.title: Bundle 7: Deployment and Troubleshooting (scenarios)
bundles.description: Scenario-based questions on upgrade and migration strategies, proxy, certificate and firewall integration issues, interpreting HAR, network and log tool output, and choosing ArcGIS Monitor 2024 components.

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to select an upgrade strategy
questions.question: A regional council's service level agreement requires the public to keep viewing maps and apps throughout an upgrade from ArcGIS Enterprise 11.1 to 11.4, although editing can pause for a day. The GIS manager also wants to validate the upgraded system before any users are moved to it. What is the most appropriate strategy?
answers: Set production to read-only, replicate it to a duplicate, upgrade and validate that, then redirect traffic
Upgrade the standby portal machine to 11.4 first while the primary portal machine keeps serving users at 11.1
Upgrade the federated ArcGIS Server sites first so services stay online, then upgrade the portal last of all
Upgrade production in place during business hours, then place it in read-only mode to validate the result
questions.explanation: Esri describes this read-only pattern for organisations with uptime requirements: production stays viewable but cannot be modified, the standby copy is upgraded and validated, and traffic is then redirected, so no content is lost. Upgrading one HA portal machine while the other serves users at the old version is not the documented procedure, and the portal must be upgraded before its servers.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Work with read-only mode in ArcGIS Enterprise

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to select an upgrade strategy
questions.question: An ArcGIS Enterprise 10.9.1 deployment with a highly available portal is to be upgraded to 11.4. The business allows a two-hour outage. A rehearsal on a cloned staging environment overran the window, mostly because the Portal for ArcGIS 11.4 setup took a long time to finish on the portal machines. What should you recommend?
answers: Use a blue-green pattern: build and upgrade a parallel environment, then switch users over to it
Uninstall Portal for ArcGIS 10.9.1 first so that the 11.4 setup runs as a faster clean installation
Upgrade to 11.0 in one window and to 11.4 in a second window so that each setup run is shorter
Skip the webgisdr backup on the night and rely on the staging rehearsal as the rollback position
questions.explanation: Esri notes that when upgrading from 10.8.1 or 10.9.1 the Portal for ArcGIS setup may take significant time, and recommends considering a blue-green pattern to minimise downtime. Uninstalling first is explicitly not required for upgrades and risks losing the existing portal, and skipping backups removes the rollback option.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Upgrade a highly available portal
source.section: Install Portal for ArcGIS on both machines

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to select an upgrade strategy
questions.question: Your organisation is moving its ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 deployment on Windows to new Windows virtual machines in a different data centre. The production environment must not be changed until the new environment has been validated. Which migration method is most appropriate?
answers: Use the WebGISDR tool to restore a backup of production into the new environment
Use Join Site to add each new machine to the existing sites, then unregister the old ones
Use distributed collaboration to replicate all content and users to the new deployment
Install 11.4 on the new machines and point them at production's content directories
questions.explanation: Join Site relies on shared storage between machines in the same site, so Esri says to use it only within the same data centre and to consider WebGISDR for a separate data centre; WebGISDR also leaves production untouched and lets you validate before switching over. Distributed collaboration is not designed for migrating content between environments.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Migrate ArcGIS Enterprise with the Join Site operation

questions.objective: Apply procedural concepts to select an upgrade strategy
questions.question: An organisation is moving its ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 deployment from Windows to Linux as part of a server refresh. The project lead proposes taking a WebGISDR backup of the Windows deployment and restoring it into a new Linux deployment over a weekend, so that item IDs and URLs are preserved. What is the appropriate response?
answers: Explain WebGISDR can't migrate to a different OS; plan a content migration to a new Linux deployment instead
Proceed, provided the organisation URL and services URLs are identical in both the Windows and Linux deployments
Use Join Site to add the Linux machines to the Windows sites, then unregister the Windows machines afterwards
Proceed, but upgrade both deployments to the same patch level first, as WebGISDR then supports a cross-OS restore
questions.explanation: Esri states that the WebGISDR migration method cannot be used to migrate to a different operating system, and Join Site also cannot be used because Windows and Linux machines cannot coexist in the same site. A Windows-to-Linux move therefore needs a content migration strategy, such as clone_items or group export and import, into a new deployment.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Migrate ArcGIS Enterprise with WebGISDR
source.section: Considerations for using the WebGISDR tool

questions.objective: Identify potential system integration issues
questions.question: The portal has just been moved behind the organisation's reverse proxy at https://gis.example.com/portal, and the WebContextURL has been set. When the administrator re-federates the ArcGIS Server site through the reverse proxy URL, the operation fails with an error saying the connection timed out. Normal map requests through the proxy work. What should you do first?
answers: Ask the network team to increase the reverse proxy's time-out so long-running requests can complete
Federate the server through the internal portal URL on port 7443 instead of the reverse proxy URL
Remove the WebContextURL property, federate the server, then set the WebContextURL property again
Enable HTTP on the portal so that the reverse proxy can forward the federation request without TLS
questions.explanation: Esri notes that after configuring a reverse proxy, a connection timed-out error during operations such as federating a server may mean the proxy's time-out is too short, and recommends increasing it. Federation must be redone using the reverse proxy URL, so bypassing it through port 7443 is not the fix.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Integrate your portal with a reverse proxy or load balancer

questions.objective: Identify potential system integration issues
questions.question: IT security wants the external organisation URL to be https://gis.example.com:8443/portal so that GIS traffic is kept apart from other sites published on port 443. You are configuring the portal behind the organisation's reverse proxy. What is the appropriate response?
answers: Explain that WebContextURL can't use a nonstandard port, so the external URL must use port 443
Set WebContextURL to the :8443 URL and add port 8443 to the portal's list of allowed ports
Change the portal's internal HTTPS port from 7443 to 8443 so it matches the external URL
Set WebContextURL to the :8443 URL and federate servers using the Web Adaptor URL instead
questions.explanation: The portal's WebContextURL property cannot use a port other than 443, so a proxy URL on :8443 cannot be the organisation URL. Changing the portal's internal port does not change this restriction.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Integrate your portal with a reverse proxy or load balancer

questions.objective: Identify potential system integration issues
questions.question: IT security has introduced a forward proxy that decrypts and re-encrypts outbound HTTPS traffic for inspection. Outbound internet access is only allowed through this proxy. Since the change, the PrintingTools service on a three-machine ArcGIS Server 11.4 site fails to print maps with ArcGIS Online basemaps. ArcGIS Server is already configured to use the proxy. What should you do?
answers: Import the proxy's root CA certificate into the OS trusted root store on each ArcGIS Server machine
Import the proxy's root CA certificate into the portal only, because federated servers inherit its trust
Ask IT security to add the three ArcGIS Server machines to the proxy's list of authenticated users
Add the ArcGIS Online domains to nonProxyHosts so the print requests bypass the inspecting proxy
questions.explanation: A decrypting proxy presents certificates from its own root CA, which ArcGIS Server does not trust by default, so the root certificate must be imported into the operating system certificate store on every machine in the site. Bypassing the proxy with nonProxyHosts fails here because direct outbound access is not allowed.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Configure a forward proxy server with ArcGIS Server

questions.objective: Identify potential system integration issues
questions.question: Security policy now requires Integrated Windows Authentication (IWA), so the ArcGIS Server site's Web Adaptor has been switched to IWA. You must now federate this site with the 11.4 portal. Which approach is supported?
answers: Use the Web Adaptor URL as the Services URL and https://gisserver.example.com:6443/arcgis for administration
Use the IWA-protected Web Adaptor URL as both the Services URL and the Administration URL during federation
Disable IWA permanently, as federation requires anonymous access through the server's ArcGIS Web Adaptor
Use port 6443 as the Services URL and the IWA-protected Web Adaptor URL as the Administration URL instead
questions.explanation: Federating with a server that uses web-tier authentication is supported as long as the Administration URL does not use web-tier authentication, which normally means using port 6443. A warning that the Services URL cannot be validated is expected in this setup.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Federate a server site

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: After the server team installs a new monitoring tool on an ArcGIS Server 11.4 machine, the ArcGIS Server service no longer starts. Running netstat -ano in PowerShell shows the new tool's process listening on TCP port 6006. The tool's vendor says its port can be changed. What is the appropriate response?
answers: Have the tool reconfigured to use another port, as ArcGIS Server needs 6006 free and can't move
Restart ArcGIS Server, as it automatically moves to port 6007 when it finds port 6006 in use
Open port 6006 in the firewall to the other site machines so that ArcGIS Server can share it
Change the ArcGIS Server HTTPS port from 6443 to 6006 in the Administrator Directory, then restart
questions.explanation: Port 6006 is used by ArcGIS Server's internal processes and must be available for the service to start; unlike ports such as 1098, ArcGIS Server cannot automatically increment to a different port when 6006 is taken. Freeing the port by moving the other application is the fix.

source.title: ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4: Ports used by ArcGIS Server

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: Users get an error at the end of a SAML sign-in to the portal. The service desk sent Esri Support a HAR file recorded in Chrome over a 40-minute session, but it contains only the requests from the final page; the redirect chain is missing. What should the service desk do?
answers: Re-capture with Preserve log enabled, clear the log, reproduce only the failing steps, then sanitise
Re-capture the whole working day with Preserve log turned off to get a larger sample of requests
Send the existing HAR as it is, since Esri Support will remove the tokens on the customer's behalf
Use Process Monitor on the client to record the browser's HTTPS requests instead of DevTools
questions.explanation: Esri's procedure is to enable Preserve log so requests survive page loads and redirects, clear existing requests, capture only the problem steps, and sanitise the HAR before sharing. Esri cannot sanitise debug files on a customer's behalf.

source.title: Esri Support: Submit HAR Debug Files to Esri Support Services for Troubleshooting and Review

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: Registering ArcGIS Monitor Agent 2024 on a server in a separate network zone fails with "Timeout awaiting 'connect' for 5000ms". On the agent machine, Test-NetConnection -ComputerName monitor.example.com -Port 30443 returns TcpTestSucceeded : False. What is the appropriate next step?
answers: Ask the network team to allow traffic from the agent machine to Monitor Server on port 30443
Re-run the registration with --agent-id, because the agent must already be registered once
Ask the network team to open ports 30001 to 30010 from the agent machine to Monitor Server
Install a second Monitor Server in the agent's network zone and register the agent with that
questions.explanation: Esri attributes this registration error to port 30443 being closed between Monitor Agent and Monitor Server, and the failed Test-NetConnection result confirms it. Ports 30001 to 30010 are used internally by Monitor Server and do not need to be opened to other machines.

source.title: Esri Support: ArcGIS Monitor: Timeout Awaiting Connect for 5000ms

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: The GIS manager wants a System Log Parser report to find the busiest and slowest services on a production ArcGIS Server site. A test run produces a report with almost no service request statistics. The site's log level is set to WARNING. What should you do?
answers: Set the log level to FINE on each server, collect at least a week of logs, then rerun the report
Rerun the report using the VerboseMode analysis type across the most recent seven days of logs
Rerun the report with an administrator account, as publisher accounts cannot read statistics
Set the log level to SEVERE so that only significant requests are recorded and then summarised
questions.explanation: Esri's guidance is to set ArcGIS Server logs to FINE on each server you want metrics for, and to log at FINE for at least a week before running System Log Parser. VerboseMode is limited to 12 hours, and a publisher account is enough to run the tool.

source.title: Esri Community: ArcGIS Server Tuning and Optimization with System Log Parser

questions.objective: Determine which ArcGIS Monitor component to use
questions.question: An ArcGIS Server machine monitored by ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1 is being replaced by a new VM in a hardware refresh. The GIS manager wants to keep the historical metrics, observers and alerts for the components that this machine's Monitor Agent collects. Which approach should you use?
answers: Disconnect the old agent, then register the new machine's agent as an existing agent using its ID
Unregister the old agent in Monitor, then register the new machine's agent as a brand-new agent
Copy the old agent's configuration store to the new machine so that it reconnects automatically
Register the new machine as a new agent, then merge the two agents' components in Monitor Server
questions.explanation: To transfer a Monitor Agent's responsibilities to another machine, you disconnect it with admin:system:disconnect and register the new installation as an existing agent with --agent-id. Unregistering an agent permanently deletes its components, metrics, observers and alerts.

source.title: ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1: Manage Monitor Agent machines

questions.objective: Determine which ArcGIS Monitor component to use
questions.question: The ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1 database repository runs on a separate PostgreSQL server managed by the DBA team. After the DBAs harden that server over the weekend, Monitor shows a database disconnected error when administrators try to access it. The DBAs suggest installing Monitor Agent on the database server to fix the connection. What is the appropriate response?
answers: Check the database is online, allows remote clients, is reachable through the firewall and the login works
Install Monitor Agent on the database server and register it, so the agent can relay the database connection
Restore the Monitor Server configuration store from backup so that the database connection is recreated
Register the PostgreSQL database as a monitored component from an existing agent so it reconnects
questions.explanation: Monitor Server connects directly to its database repository, and Esri's checklist for this error is that the database is available, configured to allow remote clients, reachable through firewall rules, and that the credentials are valid. Monitor Agent collects metrics from monitored components and does not provide Monitor Server's connection to its own repository.

source.title: ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1: Common problems and solutions

questions.objective: Determine which ArcGIS Monitor component to use
questions.question: IT security will not let users reach ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1 directly on port 30443. All web apps must be published through the existing IIS web tier on port 443, which already hosts the portal's ArcGIS Web Adaptor. What is the appropriate way to provide access?
answers: Install a dedicated ArcGIS Web Adaptor 11.4 instance and configure it for ArcGIS Monitor
Reconfigure the portal's existing Web Adaptor so that it also forwards requests to Monitor
Federate Monitor Server with the portal so it is reached through the portal's Web Adaptor
Install Monitor Agent on the IIS machine and register the web tier as a Monitor component
questions.explanation: ArcGIS Web Adaptor can front Monitor Server so users reach Monitor through the web server instead of port 30443, but Monitor requires its own dedicated Web Adaptor 11.4 instance, so the portal's Web Adaptor cannot be reused. Monitor authenticates users with its own built-in identity store.

source.title: ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1: Install and configure ArcGIS Web Adaptor with ArcGIS Monitor

questions.objective: Determine which ArcGIS Monitor component to use
questions.question: You are preparing Windows hosts for ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1 host monitoring. IT security refuses to add the ArcGIS Monitor account to the local Administrators group on these machines and asks for the minimum documented prerequisite. What should you request?
answers: Add the ArcGIS Monitor account to the Windows Performance Monitor Users group on each host
Run the Monitor Agent service as LocalSystem instead of using the ArcGIS Monitor account
Assign the ArcGIS Monitor account the Administrator role inside the Monitor web application
Register each host remotely from the Monitor Server machine's agent instead of a local agent
questions.explanation: Esri lists membership of the Windows Performance Monitor Users group for the ArcGIS Monitor account as a prerequisite for monitoring Windows hosts. Each host must also have its own Monitor Agent, so remote registration from the Monitor Server's agent is not an option.

source.title: ArcGIS Monitor 2024.1: Register Windows hosts

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: You run GIS Enterprise Reporter with With Analytics to find which services use a database due for retirement. The svc_datasets sheet lists datasets for several map services, but none for the hosted feature layers or for map services in the shared instance pool. How should you interpret this?
answers: The Admin API holds dataset details only for dedicated instance services, not hosted or shared ones
The tool lacked local machine administrator rights, which it needs to read service data sources
Those services are stopped, and the svc_datasets sheet only lists the datasets of started services
Those services use unregistered data sources, which GIS Enterprise Reporter does not report
questions.explanation: The svc_datasets sheet lists datasets referenced by dedicated instance services, because hosted and shared instance services do not include this information in the ArcGIS Server Admin API. You need another method to find their data sources. Local administrator rights add installed software and machine resource details, not dataset references.

source.title: Esri Community: GIS Enterprise Reporter: Making the Most of Services Outputs

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: A city runs ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4 with no web-tier access logs available. The GIS manager wants response-time statistics that also cover hosted feature services and vector tile services, not only ArcSOC-based services. Which System Log Parser approach suits this?
answers: Run the Info analysis type through the ArcGIS Server (File System) log query
Run the Info analysis type through the ArcGIS Server (Web) log query as an administrator
Run the ErrorsOnly analysis type through the ArcGIS Server (Web) log query
Run the Optimized analysis type against the IIS logs of the ArcGIS Web Adaptor
questions.explanation: Info log entries time requests at the framework level, including requests that are not ArcSOC-based such as hosted feature services. System Log Parser supports the Info analysis type for ArcGIS Server File System log sources only, and recommends ArcGIS Server 11.4 or later. ErrorsOnly reports warnings and errors, not response times.

source.title: Esri GitHub: System Log Parser CHANGELOG

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: A utility plans to replicate five feature classes from its enterprise geodatabase to a geodatabase in another data centre. To plan the data exchange, the architect needs each of those object classes' record counts and allocated storage. Which eGDB Health output provides this?
answers: The ObjClass sheet, listing each object class's tables, row counts and allocated storage
The FileSpace sheet, listing the size of the geodatabase's data files and transaction log
The version tree PNG, which colour-codes each version by how stale its edits have become
The LargeAttachments evaluation, which reports object classes over a storage threshold
questions.explanation: The ObjClass sheet in the Storage category reports the tables that make up each object class, their row counts and allocated storage, and shows which are versioned. The FileSpace evaluation reports the size of the whole geodatabase's files, which suits a lift-and-shift of the entire geodatabase rather than a subset.

source.title: Esri Community: Using Egdbhealth in System Design
source.section: Data Inventory and Data Exchange: Record Counts and Storage By ObjectClass

questions.objective: Interpret results and data from tools
questions.question: ArcSOC processes on an ArcGIS Server machine are being started with unexpected command lines on random nights, and the machine reboots for monthly patching. IT security wants a record that persists across reboots, written to the Windows event log so its SIEM can collect it. Which tool fits?
answers: Sysmon, configured to log process creation with command lines and parent processes
Process Monitor, left open to show real-time file system and registry activity
Fiddler, capturing the HTTP and HTTPS traffic between client apps and ArcGIS Server
System Log Parser, run with the ErrorsOnly analysis type across the patch window
questions.explanation: Sysmon is a system service and driver that stays resident across reboots and logs activity, including process creation with full command lines for current and parent processes, to the Windows event log for collection by SIEM agents. Process Monitor suits interactive, real-time capture of file system, registry and process activity, saved in its own log format.

source.title: Microsoft Learn: Sysmon

bundles.title: Bundle 8: Architectural Concepts (scenarios)
bundles.description: Scenario-based questions on workload separation, environment isolation, distributed collaboration, content delivery, backup and resiliency, and tiered architectures for ArcGIS Enterprise 11.4.

questions.objective: Determine when to use workload separation
questions.question: A regional council's emergency management dashboards rely on map and feature services that share one ArcGIS Server site with general-purpose internal services. The emergency services carry a stricter SLA. During the last storm, a surge of general staff traffic slowed the emergency services. The project sponsor asks how to stop this happening again.
